item.stdout:
# Marvin Simulator: Godot port

Agent contributors: read [PORTING.md](PORTING.md) (the translation rules, the SceneKit facade and how the port is
compared with the macOS game) and the [simulator rules](../../docs/simulator-agent-rules.md) first.

A Godot 4.7 (.NET, C#) port of the macOS game in [`apps/simulator-macos`](../simulator-macos), so that it runs on
Windows as well as macOS. The macOS game is the reference: the port mirrors its Swift code file by file over a
SceneKit/AppKit facade and is calibrated against its captures (PORTING.md). It is never modified from here.
Status and what is left: [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md).

## Setup

On a Mac or a Windows PC with git and [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/getting-started.html) (on Windows in PowerShell):

```sh
git clone --branch codex/mos-aster-racing-city https://github.com/entireio/marvin.git
cd marvin/apps/simulator-godot
mise trust
mise run setup
mise run play
```

`mise run setup` installs the tools `mise.toml` pins into mise's own folders, nothing system-wide (Godot 4.7.2 .NET,
the .NET 8 SDK, Python 3.12, Git LFS), fetches the Git LFS files the game is made from, generates the robots' meshes
from their sources (`scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py`, as the macOS build does: no macOS build needed), copies the
assets into `assets/` (gitignored), builds the C# and imports the textures and audio. The first run takes a few
minutes, mostly downloads; after a `git pull` run it again (seconds when nothing changed). `mise run play` builds the C#
and starts the game.

| Task | |
|---|---|
| `mise run play` | The game: main menu, Sandbox, Dirt Track. Flags go to the game, e.g. `mise run play -- --smoke-test /tmp/smoke` (game modes: PORTING.md, "App and game modes"); Godot's own flags go before a second `--`. On a Mac it runs Godot from `build/dev/Marvin Simulator.app`, a copy of Godot's app (an APFS clone, signed ad hoc) named after the game, so the menu bar says Marvin Simulator instead of Godot; made on first play and again when Godot changes. |
| `mise run test` | A quick headless smoke test, the town and the four robots (about 20 s on a Mac), against the same run on Godot on macOS; `mise run test -- all` runs every mode the Windows CI runs. |
| `mise run checks` | The simulation checks (no Godot). |
| `mise run export` | Release builds (below). |
| `mise run build`, `mise run godot -- ARGS` | The C# only; Godot on this project with any arguments. |

The tasks are `tools/dev.py`, in Python so that they run the same on macOS and Windows. **Without mise**, install
Godot 4.7.2 .NET (on a Mac as `~/Applications/Godot_mono.app`, otherwise set `GODOT` to the editor binary, on Windows
the `_console.exe`), the .NET 8 SDK (`~/.dotnet`, or set `DOTNET_ROOT`), Python 3 and Git LFS, and run the tasks as
`python tools/dev.py setup`, `play` and so on. The bash scripts `tools/godot`, `tools/build`, `tools/checks` and
`tools/export` (Git Bash on Windows) find Godot and .NET the same way (`tools/env.sh`: `GODOT` and `DOTNET_ROOT`, then
mise's, then `~/Applications` and `~/.dotnet`). `MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES` makes setup copy the assets from another
`Resources` folder of the macOS game that has the generated meshes, instead of generating them.

The editor runs the game from the project folder; release builds are exported (below). Keys: W A S D or the
arrows drive, Shift boosts, Space brakes, C changes the camera, P or Esc pauses, ? shows the key guide; ⌘M / ⌘R /
⌘P / ⌘1 (Ctrl on Windows) are the Simulation menu's Main Menu, Reset, Pause and Camera.

The port trades two small differences from the macOS game for frame rate at high resolutions: shadows have hard
edges, and the robots are drawn from simplified meshes where that changes less than half a pixel. Choose
Settings > Shadow quality: Exact in the game for the exact macOS look at a higher GPU cost (Fast is the default; the
choice is stored with the other settings and applies immediately; the macOS game has no such setting). For tests and
experiments the environment variable `MARVIN_SCN_CAL=Exact` selects it for any game mode, in the editor runtime and
the release builds alike, and overrides the setting (PORTING.md, "Known deviations"; `docs/performance.md`).

Settings > Graphics detail trades look for frame rate on GPUs that cannot run the full look at 60 FPS: **Max** (the
default) draws everything as before; **High** leaves out the ambient occlusion (SSAO) and simplifies four small details at
full resolution; **Medium** also draws the 3D view at 0.6 of the window's resolution and upscales it with MetalFX temporal
upscaling on macOS (FSR 2 on Windows), and lights the ground's overlay layers more simply; **Low** draws it at half the
resolution and simplifies further. The HUD and menus stay at full resolution. At 1920 x 1080 on an M2, High holds 60 FPS
with Shadow quality Fast, Medium with Exact, and Low leaves a large margin (`docs/performance.md`, "Graphics detail").
The choice is stored with the other settings and applies immediately; the two settings are independent; the macOS game
has no such setting. `MARVIN_GRAPHICS_DETAIL=Low|Medium|High|Max` selects a level for any game mode (game modes otherwise
use Max).

## Release builds

```sh
mise run export                       # on a Mac both: build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app, build/windows/MarvinSimulator.exe
mise run export -- macos              # or one platform (on Windows the default is windows)
mise run export -- windows --zip      # also build/MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64.zip, to copy to a PC
```

(`tools/export` with the same arguments, without mise.) The first export fetches the files of Godot's export templates
that the presets need (`macos.zip` and the Windows x86_64 templates, about 200 MB of the 1.2 GB
`Godot_v4.7.2-stable_mono_export_templates.tpz`) into Godot's templates folder (macOS
`~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.7.2.stable.mono/`, Windows
`%APPDATA%\Godot\export_templates\4.7.2.stable.mono\`). The export imports, exports with Godot's release template and
then runs `tools/export-verify.py` on the result,
which checks the bundle without running it (so the Windows build is checked on a Mac too): the executables'
architectures and resources, the self-contained .NET runtime and the game assemblies (built as `ExportRelease`, no
editor assemblies), the native libraries the assemblies name (only the two macOS ones, both behind an OS check), and
the pack: every raw file the game reads with `FileAccess` (`geometry.bin`, the JSON meshes and manifests, all 161
`.wav` files) byte-identical to `assets/`, every imported texture, and nothing from `reference/`, `tools/`, `docs/`,
`captures/` or `src/`.

The presets are in `export_presets.cfg`:

| | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| output | `build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app` (universal: arm64 and x86_64; .NET data folder per architecture) | `build/windows/`: `MarvinSimulator.exe`, `MarvinSimulator.console.exe` (console wrapper for terminal runs), `MarvinSimulator.pck`, `data_MarvinGodot_windows_x86_64/` (the .NET 8 win-x64 runtime and the game assemblies). Keep the four together. |
| renderer | Metal (Forward+) | Direct3D 12 (Forward+), falling back to Vulkan when D3D12 cannot start (`project.godot`: `rendering_device/driver.windows`, `fallback_to_vulkan`) |
| signing | ad-hoc, with the entitlements .NET needs (JIT, unsigned executable memory) and the ones the performance probes use (DYLD environment, library validation off); not notarised | unsigned; icon and version resources set |
| raw assets | `include_filter`: `assets/*.json, assets/*.bin`; the `.wav` files are imported with the "keep" importer, so they are packed as they are | same |

The C# is published by Godot's export (`dotnet publish`, configuration `ExportRelease`); `MarvinGodot.csproj`
optimises every configuration, so the editor runtime and the export run the same code at the same speed
(`docs/performance.md`). An exported game takes its game-mode flags with or without `--`.

### Running the macOS build

Open `build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app`, or start game modes from a terminal:

```sh
"build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app/Contents/MacOS/Marvin Simulator" --smoke-test /tmp/smoke
```

Settings, scores and logs live in `~/Library/Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/Marvin Simulator/`
(`UserDefaults.cfg`, `motocross-v4-scores.json`, `logs/godot.log`), shared with the editor runtime.

## Windows

No Windows PC has run the game yet. CI does, on a GitHub-hosted Windows runner without a GPU
(`.github/workflows/godot-windows.yml`, on every push to the port): the simulation checks, the assets generated on
Windows, the town and 12 logic modes headless, `tools/export windows` and the exported exe, and Direct3D 12 (Microsoft's
WARP software adapter) and Vulkan (Mesa lavapipe) captures. Each run's summary page lists what differs from macOS, and
the Windows build is attached to the run (`MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64`). Before that, everything that can be
checked on a Mac was: the export and its layout (above), the Windows user-interface paths (in-window menu bar, Control
shortcuts, a window fitted to a scaled screen), Godot's Vulkan renderer (through MoltenVK), the portable maths and the
thread stacks. Results: PORTING.md, "Release builds and Windows".

### Getting a build

**On Windows**: the commands in "Setup" (PowerShell, with Git for Windows and mise), then `mise run play`, or
`mise run export` for the release build in `build/windows`. CI runs exactly these on fresh Windows, macOS and Linux
runners (`.github/workflows/godot-setup.yml`).

**From a Mac**: `mise run export -- windows --zip`, copy `build/MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64.zip` to the PC and unzip
it anywhere. No installation is needed; the .NET runtime is inside.

### Running

- Double-click `MarvinSimulator.exe`. The window has the system title bar; the game's menu bar (Marvin Simulator,
  Simulation) sits in the bar below it, and the shortcuts use Ctrl: Ctrl+M main menu, Ctrl+R reset, Ctrl+P pause,
  Ctrl+1 camera, Ctrl+Q quit. On a scaled display the window keeps the game's 1280 x 820 points at the display's scale,
  made smaller (down to 900 x 640) when that does not fit the screen, as macOS does: at 125 % or 150 % on a 1080p
  display the game lays out to the shorter window.
- From a terminal use the console wrapper, which prints the log and returns the exit code:

  ```bat
  MarvinSimulator.console.exe --smoke-test out\smoke
  MarvinSimulator.console.exe --town-smoke-test out\town
  MarvinSimulator.console.exe --audio-smoke-test out\audio
  ```

  (`--` before the flags works too, but Windows PowerShell drops a bare `--`.)
- Renderer: Direct3D 12 by default; if it cannot start, Godot falls back to Vulkan. Force one with
  `--rendering-driver d3d12` or `--rendering-driver vulkan`. The Direct3D 12 Agility SDK is not shipped, so D3D12 uses
  the runtime that comes with Windows 10/11. The first start compiles shaders and is slower; later starts use Godot's
  shader cache.
- Settings, scores, logs and the shader cache: `%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\Marvin Simulator\`.

### What differs from macOS

- **Fonts.** SF Pro, SF Mono and Avenir Next Condensed are Apple's and are not shipped; Windows draws the HUD in
  Segoe UI and Consolas and the town signs in Bahnschrift. Text is measured and laid out as on the Mac (the key guide
  grows with its text, the signs shrink theirs to fit), but it looks different and has not been checked on Windows.
- **Window chrome.** The system title bar above the client area instead of the Mac's unified title bar; the menu bar
  is in the window (Windows has no global menu bar).
- **Last-digit maths.** `hypot` and the reciprocal square root behind `normalize` run managed copies of Darwin's and
  ARM's algorithms that return the same bits as macOS (`tools/checks --portable-math`). The other C library functions
  (`sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `atan2`, `exp`, `log`, `pow` ...) come from the Windows C runtime and differ from Darwin's in
  the last bit in up to a third of calls (measured in CI), so long chaotic simulations (a three-lap race with
  contacts) drift in their last digits from a macOS run, as the macOS release and debug builds do from each other.
  The generated town has the same statistics; short smoke reports (race smoke, storm races, town, entrance, people)
  are identical in CI, longer ones differ in some numbers.
- **Untested there:** a real GPU (CI renders with Direct3D 12 on WARP and with lavapipe), Windows audio output
  (WASAPI) and real display scaling.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `project.godot`, `MarvinGodot.csproj`, `MarvinGodot.sln` | The Godot project (Forward+, C#; assembly `MarvinGodot`) |
| `export_presets.cfg` | Release presets: macOS (universal), Windows Desktop (x86_64) |
| `mise.toml` | The developer setup: the pinned tools and the tasks (`tools/dev.py`) |
| `src/Core`, `src/Checks` | The simulation core (pure C#) and the port of the macOS simulation checks |
| `scripts/` | The game, mirroring the Swift sources; `scripts/SceneKit/` is the SceneKit/AppKit facade |
| `tools/` | `dev.py` (the mise tasks), `env.sh`, `godot`, `build`, `checks`, `sync-assets.py`, `export`, `export-verify.py`; `perf/` (benchmarks, `docs/performance.md`); `ci/` (the Windows CI's scripts and references) |
| `assets/`, `build/`, `reference/` | Gitignored: synced assets, exports, macOS reference captures |
# Developer setup of the Godot port with mise (https://mise.jdx.dev), on a Mac or a Windows PC with git and mise:
#
#   mise trust          # once: allow this file
#   mise run setup      # tools, Git LFS files, the game's assets, C# build, Godot import (again after a pull: seconds)
#   mise run play       # the game
#
# mise installs the tools below into its own folders (nothing system-wide) the first time a task runs. The tasks are
# tools/dev.py, which is Python so that they run the same on macOS and Windows (README.md, "Setup").
min_version = "2026.9.15"

[tool_alias]
godot-mono = "github:godotengine/godot-builds"

[tools]
dotnet = "8"      # the .NET 8 SDK (MarvinGodot.csproj targets net8.0)
python = "3.12"   # tools/ and the asset exporters (standard library only)
git-lfs = "3"     # the textures, the meshes' sources and Marvin's CAD master are Git LFS files

# Godot 4.7.2 .NET (the "mono" editor) from Godot's release builds; tools/dev.py and tools/env.sh find it with
# `mise where godot-mono`.
[tools.godot-mono]
version = "4.7.2-stable"
platforms.macos-arm64 = { asset_pattern = "Godot_v{{ version }}_mono_macos.universal.zip", bin_path = "Godot_mono.app/Contents/MacOS" }
platforms.macos-x64 = { asset_pattern = "Godot_v{{ version }}_mono_macos.universal.zip", bin_path = "Godot_mono.app/Contents/MacOS" }
platforms.windows-x64 = { asset_pattern = "Godot_v{{ version }}_mono_win64.zip", bin_path = "Godot_v{{ version }}_mono_win64" }
platforms.linux-x64 = { asset_pattern = "Godot_v{{ version }}_mono_linux_x86_64.zip", bin_path = "Godot_v{{ version }}_mono_linux_x86_64" }

[env]
DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT = "1"
DOTNET_NOLOGO = "1"

[tasks.setup]
description = "Get everything ready: Git LFS files, the game's assets (generated here, no macOS build), C# build, Godot import"
run = "python tools/dev.py setup"

[tasks.play]
description = "Build the C# and run the game; flags go to the game, e.g. mise run play -- --smoke-test /tmp/smoke"
run = "python tools/dev.py play"

[tasks.test]
description = "Quick headless smoke: the town and the four robots, compared with Godot on macOS (tools/ci/headless-modes.py)"
run = "python tools/dev.py test"

[tasks.checks]
description = "The simulation checks (C# SimulationChecks, no Godot)"
run = "python tools/dev.py checks"

[tasks.export]
description = "Release builds in build/ (macos, windows; --zip, --debug); downloads the export templates when missing"
run = "python tools/dev.py export"

[tasks.build]
description = "Build the C# (MarvinGodot and MarvinCore)"
run = "python tools/dev.py build"

[tasks.godot]
description = "Godot on this project with any arguments, e.g. mise run godot -- --headless --import"
run = "python tools/dev.py godot"
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The Godot port's developer tasks, the same on macOS and Windows. mise.toml runs them (README.md, "Setup"):

    mise run setup                      # Git LFS files, the game's assets, C# build, Godot import (idempotent)
    mise run play [-- FLAGS]            # build, then the game; FLAGS go to the game (Godot's own before a second --)
    mise run test [-- MODES|all]        # quick headless smoke (tools/ci/headless-modes.py)
    mise run checks [-- ARGS]           # the simulation checks (no Godot)
    mise run export [-- macos|windows] [--zip] [--debug]   # release builds; fetches the export templates when missing
    mise run build                      # the C#
    mise run godot -- ARGS              # Godot on this project with any arguments

Without mise: python tools/dev.py TASK [ARGS]. Godot and .NET are $GODOT and $DOTNET_ROOT when set, otherwise the
versions mise.toml pins (`mise where`), otherwise ~/Applications/Godot_mono.app and ~/.dotnet, the order tools/env.sh
uses for the bash scripts. Standard library only.
"""
import http.client
import io
import os
import platform
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent  # apps/simulator-godot
REPO = ROOT.parent.parent
MAC_RESOURCES = REPO / "apps" / "simulator-macos" / "Resources"
MARVIN_STEP = "hardware/mechanical/step/marvin_robot.step"
LFS_INCLUDE = f"apps/simulator-macos/Resources/**,{MARVIN_STEP}"  # what the game is made from
LFS_POINTER = b"version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/"
GODOT_VERSION = "4.7.2.stable.mono"
SMOKE_MODES = "town-statistics,character-smoke-test"
WINDOWS, MACOS = os.name == "nt", sys.platform == "darwin"
EXE = ".exe" if WINDOWS else ""
PRESETS = {"macos": ("macOS", "build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app"),
           "windows": ("Windows Desktop", "build/windows/MarvinSimulator.exe")}
# What each preset needs from the export templates besides version.txt and the ICU data.
TEMPLATES = {("macos", "release"): ["macos.zip"], ("macos", "debug"): ["macos.zip"],
             ("windows", "release"): ["windows_release_x86_64.exe", "windows_release_x86_64_console.exe"],
             ("windows", "debug"): ["windows_debug_x86_64.exe", "windows_debug_x86_64_console.exe"]}


def say(message):
    print(f"==> {message}", flush=True)


def die(message):
    print(f"dev.py: {message}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    sys.exit(1)


def run(cmd, check=True, **kwargs):
    cmd = [str(c) for c in cmd]
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, **kwargs)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        sys.exit(130)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        die(f"{' '.join([Path(cmd[0]).name, *cmd[1:3]])} ... failed (exit {proc.returncode})")
    return proc


def tail(path, lines=40):
    return "\n".join(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()[-lines:])


# --- Tools -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def mise_where(tool):
    """The install folder of a tool that mise.toml pins, or None (no mise, config not trusted, tool not installed)."""
    mise = shutil.which("mise")
    if not mise:
        return None
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run([mise, "where", tool], cwd=ROOT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True,
                              text=True, timeout=120)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    lines = proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()
    folder = Path(lines[-1].strip()) if proc.returncode == 0 and lines else None
    return folder if folder and folder.is_dir() else None


def godot_in(folder):
    """The Godot .NET editor binary in an unpacked release (on Windows the console variant, which prints the log)."""
    if MACOS:
        candidates = [folder / "Godot_mono.app" / "Contents" / "MacOS" / "Godot"]
    else:
        pattern = "Godot_v*_mono_*_console.exe" if WINDOWS else "Godot_v*_mono_linux*"
        candidates = [c for c in sorted(folder.glob(pattern)) + sorted(folder.glob(f"*/{pattern}"))
                      if WINDOWS or re.search(r"\.(x86_64|arm64)$", c.name)]
    return next((c for c in candidates if c.is_file()), None)


def find_godot():
    if os.environ.get("GODOT"):
        godot = Path(os.environ["GODOT"])
        if not godot.is_file():
            die(f"GODOT is set to {godot}, which does not exist")
        return godot
    folder = mise_where("godot-mono")
    godot = godot_in(folder) if folder else None
    for apps in ([Path.home() / "Applications", Path("/Applications")] if MACOS and not godot else []):
        godot = godot or godot_in(apps)
    if not godot:
        die("Godot 4.7.2 .NET not found: run the tasks with mise (mise run setup installs it), "
            "or set GODOT to the editor binary (README.md)")
    return godot


def setup_dotnet():
    """Puts the .NET SDK on PATH and in DOTNET_ROOT, for dotnet and for Godot, which loads .NET from there."""
    root = os.environ.get("DOTNET_ROOT")
    if not root:
        for folder in (mise_where("dotnet"), Path.home() / ".dotnet"):
            if folder and (folder / f"dotnet{EXE}").is_file():
                root = str(folder)
                break
    if root:
        os.environ["DOTNET_ROOT"] = root
        paths = [os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(p)) for p in os.environ.get("PATH", "").split(os.pathsep) if p]
        if os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(root)) not in paths:
            os.environ["PATH"] = root + os.pathsep + os.environ.get("PATH", "")
    dotnet = shutil.which("dotnet")
    if not dotnet:
        die(".NET SDK not found: run the tasks with mise (mise run setup installs it), or set DOTNET_ROOT")
    return dotnet


def godot_version(godot):
    proc = subprocess.run([str(godot), "--headless", "--version"], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True,
                          text=True, errors="replace", timeout=300)
    lines = [line.strip() for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    return lines[-1] if lines else ""


# --- Setup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def lfs_pointers():
    """The files the game is made from that are still Git LFS pointers (a clone made without Git LFS)."""
    pointers = []
    for path in [*MAC_RESOURCES.rglob("*"), REPO / MARVIN_STEP]:
        try:
            if path.is_file() and path.stat().st_size < 1024:
                with open(path, "rb") as f:
                    if f.read(len(LFS_POINTER)) == LFS_POINTER:
                        pointers.append(path)
        except OSError:
            pass
    return pointers


def fetch_lfs(pointers):
    say(f"Git LFS: fetching {len(pointers)} files (textures, mesh sources, Marvin's CAD master)")
    git = shutil.which("git") or die("git not found")
    if subprocess.run([git, "lfs", "version"], capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
        die("Git LFS not found: run the tasks with mise (it provides Git LFS), or install Git LFS")
    configured = subprocess.run([git, "config", "--get", "filter.lfs.process"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True,
                                text=True).stdout.strip()
    config, hooks = [], None
    if not configured:
        # This git has no Git LFS (Apple's git on a new Mac). Use mise's git-lfs for this command only and leave
        # .git/config and .git/hooks alone, so that git keeps working where git-lfs is not on PATH (Git LFS's hooks,
        # which `git lfs pull` would install, stop `git push` without it).
        hooks = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="marvin-lfs-hooks-")
        config = ["-c", "filter.lfs.clean=git-lfs clean -- %f", "-c", "filter.lfs.smudge=git-lfs smudge -- %f",
                  "-c", "filter.lfs.process=git-lfs filter-process", "-c", "filter.lfs.required=true",
                  "-c", f"core.hooksPath={hooks}"]
    try:
        run([git, *config, "lfs", "pull", f"--include={LFS_INCLUDE}"], cwd=REPO)
        if config:

            # files written in the same second as its index for changed ones.
            time.sleep(1.5)
            subprocess.run([git, *config, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no"], cwd=REPO,
                           capture_output=True)
    finally:
        if hooks:
            shutil.rmtree(hooks, ignore_errors=True)
    left = lfs_pointers()
    if left:
        die(f"Git LFS: {len(left)} files are still pointers, e.g. {left[0]}")
    if not configured:
        print("    (Your git has no Git LFS, so a later `git pull` leaves changed LFS files as pointers until the next "
              "`mise run setup`.)", flush=True)

        pointers = lfs_pointers()
        if pointers:
            fetch_lfs(pointers)
        else:
            say("Git LFS: files present")
        say("Assets: the robots' meshes (scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py, skipped when up to date)")

        env["MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES"] = str(MAC_RESOURCES)  # this checkout's, also in a git worktree

def cmd_play(args):

    godot = dev_app(godot) if MACOS else godot
    # Flags are the game's (after "--", OS.GetCmdlineUserArgs); with a "--" of their own, Godot's come before it.
    args = args if not args or "--" in args else ["--", *args]

DEV_APP = ROOT / "build" / "dev" / "Marvin Simulator.app"
DEV_APP_VERSION = "1"  # bump when dev_app changes what it makes


def dev_app(godot):
    """The editor binary in a copy of Godot's app named Marvin Simulator, so that the menu bar and the Dock show the
    game's name and icon (macOS takes them from the app's Info.plist, which Godot cannot change at run time; exports
    have their own). The copy is an APFS clone (no extra disk space) with a new Info.plist and icon, signed ad hoc.
    Remade when Godot or the icon changes; on any failure, play runs Godot's own app."""
    source = godot.parent.parent.parent
    if source.suffix != ".app" or source == DEV_APP:
        return godot
    icon = ROOT / "assets" / "Icons" / "AppIconLight.png"
    stamp_file = DEV_APP.parent / "dev-app.stamp"  # outside the signed bundle
    stamp = "\n".join([DEV_APP_VERSION, str(source), str((source / "Contents" / "Info.plist").stat().st_mtime_ns),
                       str(icon.stat().st_mtime_ns) if icon.is_file() else "-"])
    binary = DEV_APP / "Contents" / "MacOS" / godot.name
    if binary.is_file() and stamp_file.is_file() and stamp_file.read_text() == stamp:
        return binary
    say(f"Making {DEV_APP.relative_to(ROOT)} (Godot's app with the game's name and icon)")
    try:
        shutil.rmtree(DEV_APP, ignore_errors=True)
        DEV_APP.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        quiet = {"stdout": subprocess.DEVNULL, "stderr": subprocess.PIPE, "text": True}
        if subprocess.run(["cp", "-cR", source, DEV_APP], **quiet).returncode:  # clone; a copy off APFS
            shutil.copytree(source, DEV_APP, symlinks=True)
        plist = DEV_APP / "Contents" / "Info.plist"
        steps = [["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleName", "-string", "Marvin Simulator", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleDisplayName", "-string", "Marvin Simulator", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleIdentifier", "-string", "io.entire.marvin.simulator.godot.dev", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-remove", "CFBundleDocumentTypes", plist]]
        if icon.is_file():
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
                iconset = Path(tmp) / "Marvin.iconset"
                iconset.mkdir()
                for size in (16, 32, 128, 256, 512):
                    for scale in (1, 2):
                        name = f"icon_{size}x{size}{'@2x' if scale == 2 else ''}.png"
                        run(["sips", "-z", size * scale, size * scale, icon, "--out", iconset / name], **quiet)
                run(["iconutil", "-c", "icns", iconset, "-o", DEV_APP / "Contents" / "Resources" / "Marvin.icns"],
                    **quiet)
            # The asset catalog's icon (CFBundleIconName) takes precedence over CFBundleIconFile.
            steps += [["plutil", "-remove", "CFBundleIconName", plist],
                      ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleIconFile", "-string", "Marvin.icns", plist]]
        for step in steps:
            subprocess.run(step, **quiet)  # -remove of a missing key fails harmlessly
        subprocess.run(["xattr", "-dr", "com.apple.quarantine", DEV_APP], **quiet)
        # Only the outer bundle changed: re-sign it ad hoc, keeping Godot's entitlements and hardened runtime.
        signed = subprocess.run(["codesign", "--force", "--sign", "-", "--preserve-metadata=entitlements,flags",
                                 DEV_APP], **quiet)
        if signed.returncode:
            raise OSError(signed.stderr.strip())
        stamp_file.write_text(stamp)
        return binary
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError, SystemExit) as error:
        print(f"    warning: {error or 'failed'}; playing in Godot's own app", flush=True)
        shutil.rmtree(DEV_APP, ignore_errors=True)

# --- Export ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class RangeReader(io.RawIOBase):
    """A remote file read with HTTP range requests, so that zipfile downloads only the members it extracts."""

    def __init__(self, url):
        self.url, self.pos = url, 0
        with self._get(0, 0) as response:
            if response.status != 206:
                raise OSError(f"HTTP {response.status} to a range request")
            self.size = int(response.headers["Content-Range"].rsplit("/", 1)[1])

    def _get(self, first, last):
        request = urllib.request.Request(self.url, headers={"Range": f"bytes={first}-{last}",
                                                            "User-Agent": "marvin-simulator-godot"})
        return urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60)

    def readable(self):
        return True

    def seekable(self):
        return True

    def tell(self):
        return self.pos

    def seek(self, offset, whence=io.SEEK_SET):
        self.pos = {io.SEEK_SET: 0, io.SEEK_CUR: self.pos, io.SEEK_END: self.size}[whence] + offset
        return self.pos

    def readinto(self, buffer):
        end = min(self.pos + len(buffer), self.size)
        if end <= self.pos:
            return 0
        for attempt in range(5):
            try:
                with self._get(self.pos, end - 1) as response:
                    if response.status != 206:
                        raise OSError(f"HTTP {response.status} to a range request")
                    data = response.read()
                break
            except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException):
                if attempt == 4:
                    raise
                time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
        buffer[:len(data)] = data
        self.pos += len(data)
        return len(data)


def templates_folder(template_version):
    if MACOS:
        base = Path.home() / "Library" / "Application Support" / "Godot"
    elif WINDOWS:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("APPDATA") or Path.home() / "AppData" / "Roaming") / "Godot"
    else:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME") or Path.home() / ".local" / "share") / "godot"
    return base / "export_templates" / template_version


def ensure_templates(folder, template_version, needed):
    """Fetches the export template files the presets need from Godot's release archive (1.2 GB for every platform;
    only the needed members, about 200 MB for both presets, are downloaded)."""
    missing = [name for name in ["icudt_godot.dat", *needed, "version.txt"] if not (folder / name).is_file()]
    if not missing:
        return
    match = re.match(r"(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\.([a-z0-9]+)\.mono$", template_version)
    if not match:
        die(f"unexpected Godot version {template_version}")
    tag = f"{match[1]}-{match[2]}"
    url = f"https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/{tag}/Godot_v{tag}_mono_export_templates.tpz"
    say(f"Export templates {template_version}: fetching {', '.join(missing)} into {folder}")
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    whole = None
    try:
        source = io.BufferedReader(RangeReader(url), buffer_size=8 << 20)
    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:
        print(f"    no range requests ({error}): downloading the whole archive", flush=True)
        fd, whole = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".tpz")
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as f, urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as response:
            shutil.copyfileobj(response, f, 1 << 20)
        source = open(whole, "rb")
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(source) as archive:
            for name in missing:  # version.txt last: Godot takes the folder for complete once it is there
                info = archive.getinfo(f"templates/{name}")
                print(f"    {name} ({info.file_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)", flush=True)
                partial = folder / f"{name}.part"
                with archive.open(info) as src, open(partial, "wb") as dst:  # zipfile checks the CRC
                    shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst, 1 << 20)
                os.replace(partial, folder / name)
    finally:
        source.close()
        if whole:
            os.unlink(whole)


EXPORT_HELP = """mise run export [-- macos|windows] [--zip] [--debug]   (python tools/dev.py export ...)
  Release builds: build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app, build/windows/MarvinSimulator.exe (default: both on a Mac,
  windows elsewhere), checked by tools/export-verify.py. --zip also packs build/MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64.zip to
  copy to a PC; --debug uses the debug engine template (same C#, ExportDebug). Fetches the Godot export templates when
  they are missing."""


def cmd_export(args):
    platforms, mode, pack = [], "release", False
    for arg in args:
        if arg in PRESETS:
            platforms.append(arg)
        elif arg == "--debug":
            mode = "debug"
        elif arg == "--zip":
            pack = True
        elif arg in ("-h", "--help"):
            print(EXPORT_HELP)
            return 0
        else:
            die(f"export: unknown argument {arg}\n{EXPORT_HELP}")
    platforms = platforms or (["macos", "windows"] if MACOS else ["windows"])
    if not (ROOT / "assets" / "Marvin" / "geometry.bin").is_file():
        die("assets/ is missing: run mise run setup first")
    setup_dotnet()
    godot = find_godot()
    version = godot_version(godot)
    match = re.match(r"(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?\.[a-z0-9]+\.mono)", version)
    if not match:
        die(f"{godot} is not a Godot .NET editor (version {version!r})")
    folder = templates_folder(match[1])
    ensure_templates(folder, match[1], sorted({n for p in platforms for n in TEMPLATES[(p, mode)]}))

    # Imports first: the export packs the imported textures and the raw .wav files (importer "keep", sync-assets.py).
    import_project(godot)
    status = 0
    for name in platforms:
        preset, out = PRESETS[name]
        folder_out = (ROOT / out).parent
        shutil.rmtree(folder_out, ignore_errors=True)
        folder_out.mkdir(parents=True)
        log = ROOT / "build" / f"export-{name}.log"
        say(f"Exporting {preset} ({mode}) -> {out}")
        with open(log, "wb") as f:
            proc = run([godot, "--headless", "--path", ROOT, f"--export-{mode}", preset, ROOT / out], check=False,
                       stdout=f, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            print(tail(log), file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"dev.py: {preset} export failed, log: {log}", file=sys.stderr)
            status = 1
            continue
        errors = [line for line in log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
                  if re.search(r"(^|m)(ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR):", line)]
        if errors:
            print("\n".join(errors), file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"dev.py: {preset} export logged errors, log: {log}", file=sys.stderr)
            status = 1
        if run([sys.executable, ROOT / "tools" / "export-verify.py", folder_out], check=False, cwd=ROOT).returncode:
            status = 1
        if pack and name == "windows":
            archive = ROOT / "build" / "MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64"
            Path(f"{archive}.zip").unlink(missing_ok=True)
            shutil.make_archive(str(archive), "zip", folder_out)
            print("Packed build/MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64.zip", flush=True)
    return status


TASKS = {"setup": cmd_setup, "play": cmd_play, "test": cmd_test, "checks": cmd_checks, "export": cmd_export,
         "build": cmd_build, "godot": cmd_godot}


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2 or sys.argv[1] not in TASKS:
        print(__doc__.strip())
        return 0 if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help") else 2
    return TASKS[sys.argv[1]](sys.argv[2:])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Marvin Simulator: Godot port

Agent contributors: read [PORTING.md](PORTING.md) (the translation rules, the SceneKit facade and how the port is
compared with the macOS game) and the [simulator rules](../../docs/simulator-agent-rules.md) first.

A Godot 4.7 (.NET, C#) port of the macOS game in [`apps/simulator-macos`](../simulator-macos), so that it runs on
Windows as well as macOS. The macOS game is the reference: the port mirrors its Swift code file by file over a
SceneKit/AppKit facade and is calibrated against its captures (PORTING.md). It is never modified from here.
Status and what is left: [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md).

## Setup

On a Mac or a Windows PC with git and [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/getting-started.html) (on Windows in PowerShell):

```sh
git clone --branch codex/mos-aster-racing-city https://github.com/entireio/marvin.git
cd marvin/apps/simulator-godot
mise trust
mise run setup
mise run play
```

`mise run setup` installs the tools `mise.toml` pins into mise's own folders, nothing system-wide (Godot 4.7.2 .NET,
the .NET 8 SDK, Python 3.12, Git LFS), fetches the Git LFS files the game is made from, generates the robots' meshes
from their sources (`scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py`, as the macOS build does: no macOS build needed), copies the
assets into `assets/` (gitignored), builds the C# and imports the textures and audio. The first run takes a few
minutes, mostly downloads; after a `git pull` run it again (seconds when nothing changed). `mise run play` builds the C#
and starts the game.

| Task | |
|---|---|
| `mise run play` | The game: main menu, Sandbox, Dirt Track. Flags go to the game, e.g. `mise run play -- --smoke-test /tmp/smoke` (game modes: PORTING.md, "App and game modes"); Godot's own flags go before a second `--`. On a Mac it runs Godot from `build/dev/Marvin Simulator.app`, a copy of Godot's app (an APFS clone, signed ad hoc) named after the game, so the menu bar says Marvin Simulator instead of Godot; made on first play and again when Godot changes. |
| `mise run test` | A quick headless smoke test, the town and the four robots (about 20 s on a Mac), against the same run on Godot on macOS; `mise run test -- all` runs every mode the Windows CI runs. |
| `mise run checks` | The simulation checks (no Godot). |
| `mise run export` | Release builds (below). |
| `mise run build`, `mise run godot -- ARGS` | The C# only; Godot on this project with any arguments. |

The tasks are `tools/dev.py`, in Python so that they run the same on macOS and Windows. **Without mise**, install
Godot 4.7.2 .NET (on a Mac as `~/Applications/Godot_mono.app`, otherwise set `GODOT` to the editor binary, on Windows
the `_console.exe`), the .NET 8 SDK (`~/.dotnet`, or set `DOTNET_ROOT`), Python 3 and Git LFS, and run the tasks as
`python tools/dev.py setup`, `play` and so on. The bash scripts `tools/godot`, `tools/build`, `tools/checks` and
`tools/export` (Git Bash on Windows) find Godot and .NET the same way (`tools/env.sh`: `GODOT` and `DOTNET_ROOT`, then
mise's, then `~/Applications` and `~/.dotnet`). `MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES` makes setup copy the assets from another
`Resources` folder of the macOS game that has the generated meshes, instead of generating them.

The editor runs the game from the project folder; release builds are exported (below). Keys: W A S D or the
arrows drive, Shift boosts, Space brakes, C changes the camera, P or Esc pauses, ? shows the key guide; ⌘M / ⌘R /
⌘P / ⌘1 (Ctrl on Windows) are the Simulation menu's Main Menu, Reset, Pause and Camera.

The port trades two small differences from the macOS game for frame rate at high resolutions: shadows have hard
edges, and the robots are drawn from simplified meshes where that changes less than half a pixel. Choose
Settings > Shadow quality: Exact in the game for the exact macOS look at a higher GPU cost (Fast is the default; the
choice is stored with the other settings and applies immediately; the macOS game has no such setting). For tests and
experiments the environment variable `MARVIN_SCN_CAL=Exact` selects it for any game mode, in the editor runtime and
the release builds alike, and overrides the setting (PORTING.md, "Known deviations"; `docs/performance.md`).

Settings > Graphics detail trades look for frame rate on GPUs that cannot run the full look at 60 FPS: **Max** (the
default) draws everything as before; **High** leaves out the ambient occlusion (SSAO) and simplifies four small details at
full resolution; **Medium** also draws the 3D view at 0.6 of the window's resolution and upscales it with MetalFX temporal
upscaling on macOS (FSR 2 on Windows), and lights the ground's overlay layers more simply; **Low** draws it at half the
resolution and simplifies further. The HUD and menus stay at full resolution. At 1920 x 1080 on an M2, High holds 60 FPS
with Shadow quality Fast, Medium with Exact, and Low leaves a large margin (`docs/performance.md`, "Graphics detail").
The choice is stored with the other settings and applies immediately; the two settings are independent; the macOS game
has no such setting. `MARVIN_GRAPHICS_DETAIL=Low|Medium|High|Max` selects a level for any game mode (game modes otherwise
use Max).

## Release builds

```sh
mise run export                       # on a Mac both: build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app, build/windows/MarvinSimulator.exe
mise run export -- macos              # or one platform (on Windows the default is windows)
mise run export -- windows --zip      # also build/MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64.zip, to copy to a PC
```

(`tools/export` with the same arguments, without mise.) The first export fetches the files of Godot's export templates
that the presets need (`macos.zip` and the Windows x86_64 templates, about 200 MB of the 1.2 GB
`Godot_v4.7.2-stable_mono_export_templates.tpz`) into Godot's templates folder (macOS
`~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.7.2.stable.mono/`, Windows
`%APPDATA%\Godot\export_templates\4.7.2.stable.mono\`). The export imports, exports with Godot's release template and
then runs `tools/export-verify.py` on the result,
which checks the bundle without running it (so the Windows build is checked on a Mac too): the executables'
architectures and resources, the self-contained .NET runtime and the game assemblies (built as `ExportRelease`, no
editor assemblies), the native libraries the assemblies name (only the two macOS ones, both behind an OS check), and
the pack: every raw file the game reads with `FileAccess` (`geometry.bin`, the JSON meshes and manifests, all 161
`.wav` files) byte-identical to `assets/`, every imported texture, and nothing from `reference/`, `tools/`, `docs/`,
`captures/` or `src/`.

The presets are in `export_presets.cfg`:

| | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| output | `build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app` (universal: arm64 and x86_64; .NET data folder per architecture) | `build/windows/`: `MarvinSimulator.exe`, `MarvinSimulator.console.exe` (console wrapper for terminal runs), `MarvinSimulator.pck`, `data_MarvinGodot_windows_x86_64/` (the .NET 8 win-x64 runtime and the game assemblies). Keep the four together. |
| renderer | Metal (Forward+) | Direct3D 12 (Forward+), falling back to Vulkan when D3D12 cannot start (`project.godot`: `rendering_device/driver.windows`, `fallback_to_vulkan`) |
| signing | ad-hoc, with the entitlements .NET needs (JIT, unsigned executable memory) and the ones the performance probes use (DYLD environment, library validation off); not notarised | unsigned; icon and version resources set |
| raw assets | `include_filter`: `assets/*.json, assets/*.bin`; the `.wav` files are imported with the "keep" importer, so they are packed as they are | same |

The C# is published by Godot's export (`dotnet publish`, configuration `ExportRelease`); `MarvinGodot.csproj`
optimises every configuration, so the editor runtime and the export run the same code at the same speed
(`docs/performance.md`). An exported game takes its game-mode flags with or without `--`.

### Running the macOS build

Open `build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app`, or start game modes from a terminal:

```sh
"build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app/Contents/MacOS/Marvin Simulator" --smoke-test /tmp/smoke
```

Settings, scores and logs live in `~/Library/Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/Marvin Simulator/`
(`UserDefaults.cfg`, `motocross-v4-scores.json`, `logs/godot.log`), shared with the editor runtime.

## Windows

No Windows PC has run the game yet. CI does, on a GitHub-hosted Windows runner without a GPU
(`.github/workflows/godot-windows.yml`, on every push to the port): the simulation checks, the assets generated on
Windows, the town and 12 logic modes headless, `tools/export windows` and the exported exe, and Direct3D 12 (Microsoft's
WARP software adapter) and Vulkan (Mesa lavapipe) captures. Each run's summary page lists what differs from macOS, and
the Windows build is attached to the run (`MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64`). Before that, everything that can be
checked on a Mac was: the export and its layout (above), the Windows user-interface paths (in-window menu bar, Control
shortcuts, a window fitted to a scaled screen), Godot's Vulkan renderer (through MoltenVK), the portable maths and the
thread stacks. Results: PORTING.md, "Release builds and Windows".

### Getting a build

**On Windows**: the commands in "Setup" (PowerShell, with Git for Windows and mise), then `mise run play`, or
`mise run export` for the release build in `build/windows`. CI runs exactly these on fresh Windows, macOS and Linux
runners (`.github/workflows/godot-setup.yml`).

**From a Mac**: `mise run export -- windows --zip`, copy `build/MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64.zip` to the PC and unzip
it anywhere. No installation is needed; the .NET runtime is inside.

### Running

- Double-click `MarvinSimulator.exe`. The window has the system title bar; the game's menu bar (Marvin Simulator,
  Simulation) sits in the bar below it, and the shortcuts use Ctrl: Ctrl+M main menu, Ctrl+R reset, Ctrl+P pause,
  Ctrl+1 camera, Ctrl+Q quit. On a scaled display the window keeps the game's 1280 x 820 points at the display's scale,
  made smaller (down to 900 x 640) when that does not fit the screen, as macOS does: at 125 % or 150 % on a 1080p
  display the game lays out to the shorter window.
- From a terminal use the console wrapper, which prints the log and returns the exit code:

  ```bat
  MarvinSimulator.console.exe --smoke-test out\smoke
  MarvinSimulator.console.exe --town-smoke-test out\town
  MarvinSimulator.console.exe --audio-smoke-test out\audio
  ```

  (`--` before the flags works too, but Windows PowerShell drops a bare `--`.)
- Renderer: Direct3D 12 by default; if it cannot start, Godot falls back to Vulkan. Force one with
  `--rendering-driver d3d12` or `--rendering-driver vulkan`. The Direct3D 12 Agility SDK is not shipped, so D3D12 uses
  the runtime that comes with Windows 10/11. The first start compiles shaders and is slower; later starts use Godot's
  shader cache.
- Settings, scores, logs and the shader cache: `%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\Marvin Simulator\`.

### What differs from macOS

- **Fonts.** SF Pro, SF Mono and Avenir Next Condensed are Apple's and are not shipped; Windows draws the HUD in
  Segoe UI and Consolas and the town signs in Bahnschrift. Text is measured and laid out as on the Mac (the key guide
  grows with its text, the signs shrink theirs to fit), but it looks different and has not been checked on Windows.
- **Window chrome.** The system title bar above the client area instead of the Mac's unified title bar; the menu bar
  is in the window (Windows has no global menu bar).
- **Last-digit maths.** `hypot` and the reciprocal square root behind `normalize` run managed copies of Darwin's and
  ARM's algorithms that return the same bits as macOS (`tools/checks --portable-math`). The other C library functions
  (`sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `atan2`, `exp`, `log`, `pow` ...) come from the Windows C runtime and differ from Darwin's in
  the last bit in up to a third of calls (measured in CI), so long chaotic simulations (a three-lap race with
  contacts) drift in their last digits from a macOS run, as the macOS release and debug builds do from each other.
  The generated town has the same statistics; short smoke reports (race smoke, storm races, town, entrance, people)
  are identical in CI, longer ones differ in some numbers.
- **Untested there:** a real GPU (CI renders with Direct3D 12 on WARP and with lavapipe), Windows audio output
  (WASAPI) and real display scaling.

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `project.godot`, `MarvinGodot.csproj`, `MarvinGodot.sln` | The Godot project (Forward+, C#; assembly `MarvinGodot`) |

| `tools/` | `dev.py` (the mise tasks), `env.sh`, `godot`, `build`, `checks`, `sync-assets.py`, `export`, `export-verify.py`; `perf/` (benchmarks, `docs/performance.md`); `ci/` (the Windows CI's scripts and references) |
| `assets/`, `build/`, `reference/` | Gitignored: synced assets, exports, macOS reference captures |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The Godot port's developer tasks, the same on macOS and Windows. mise.toml runs them (README.md, "Setup"):

    mise run setup                      # Git LFS files, the game's assets, C# build, Godot import (idempotent)
    mise run play [-- FLAGS]            # build, then the game; FLAGS go to the game (Godot's own before a second --)
    mise run test [-- MODES|all]        # quick headless smoke (tools/ci/headless-modes.py)
    mise run checks [-- ARGS]           # the simulation checks (no Godot)
    mise run export [-- macos|windows] [--zip] [--debug]   # release builds; fetches the export templates when missing
    mise run build                      # the C#
    mise run godot -- ARGS              # Godot on this project with any arguments

Without mise: python tools/dev.py TASK [ARGS]. Godot and .NET are $GODOT and $DOTNET_ROOT when set, otherwise the
versions mise.toml pins (`mise where`), otherwise ~/Applications/Godot_mono.app and ~/.dotnet, the order tools/env.sh
uses for the bash scripts. Standard library only.
"""
import http.client
import io
import os
import platform
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent  # apps/simulator-godot
REPO = ROOT.parent.parent
MAC_RESOURCES = REPO / "apps" / "simulator-macos" / "Resources"
MARVIN_STEP = "hardware/mechanical/step/marvin_robot.step"
LFS_INCLUDE = f"apps/simulator-macos/Resources/**,{MARVIN_STEP}"  # what the game is made from
LFS_POINTER = b"version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/"
GODOT_VERSION = "4.7.2.stable.mono"
SMOKE_MODES = "town-statistics,character-smoke-test"
WINDOWS, MACOS = os.name == "nt", sys.platform == "darwin"
EXE = ".exe" if WINDOWS else ""
PRESETS = {"macos": ("macOS", "build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app"),
           "windows": ("Windows Desktop", "build/windows/MarvinSimulator.exe")}
# What each preset needs from the export templates besides version.txt and the ICU data.
TEMPLATES = {("macos", "release"): ["macos.zip"], ("macos", "debug"): ["macos.zip"],
             ("windows", "release"): ["windows_release_x86_64.exe", "windows_release_x86_64_console.exe"],
             ("windows", "debug"): ["windows_debug_x86_64.exe", "windows_debug_x86_64_console.exe"]}


def say(message):
    print(f"==> {message}", flush=True)


def die(message):
    print(f"dev.py: {message}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    sys.exit(1)


def run(cmd, check=True, **kwargs):
    cmd = [str(c) for c in cmd]
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, **kwargs)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        sys.exit(130)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        die(f"{' '.join([Path(cmd[0]).name, *cmd[1:3]])} ... failed (exit {proc.returncode})")
    return proc


def tail(path, lines=40):
    return "\n".join(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()[-lines:])


# --- Tools -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def mise_where(tool):
    """The install folder of a tool that mise.toml pins, or None (no mise, config not trusted, tool not installed)."""
    mise = shutil.which("mise")
    if not mise:
        return None
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run([mise, "where", tool], cwd=ROOT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True,
                              text=True, timeout=120)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    lines = proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()
    folder = Path(lines[-1].strip()) if proc.returncode == 0 and lines else None
    return folder if folder and folder.is_dir() else None


def godot_in(folder):
    """The Godot .NET editor binary in an unpacked release (on Windows the console variant, which prints the log)."""
    if MACOS:
        candidates = [folder / "Godot_mono.app" / "Contents" / "MacOS" / "Godot"]
    else:
        pattern = "Godot_v*_mono_*_console.exe" if WINDOWS else "Godot_v*_mono_linux*"
        candidates = [c for c in sorted(folder.glob(pattern)) + sorted(folder.glob(f"*/{pattern}"))
                      if WINDOWS or re.search(r"\.(x86_64|arm64)$", c.name)]
    return next((c for c in candidates if c.is_file()), None)


def find_godot():
    if os.environ.get("GODOT"):
        godot = Path(os.environ["GODOT"])
        if not godot.is_file():
            die(f"GODOT is set to {godot}, which does not exist")
        return godot
    folder = mise_where("godot-mono")
    godot = godot_in(folder) if folder else None
    for apps in ([Path.home() / "Applications", Path("/Applications")] if MACOS and not godot else []):
        godot = godot or godot_in(apps)
    if not godot:
        die("Godot 4.7.2 .NET not found: run the tasks with mise (mise run setup installs it), "
            "or set GODOT to the editor binary (README.md)")
    return godot


def setup_dotnet():
    """Puts the .NET SDK on PATH and in DOTNET_ROOT, for dotnet and for Godot, which loads .NET from there."""
    root = os.environ.get("DOTNET_ROOT")
    if not root:
        for folder in (mise_where("dotnet"), Path.home() / ".dotnet"):
            if folder and (folder / f"dotnet{EXE}").is_file():
                root = str(folder)
                break
    if root:
        os.environ["DOTNET_ROOT"] = root
        paths = [os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(p)) for p in os.environ.get("PATH", "").split(os.pathsep) if p]
        if os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(root)) not in paths:
            os.environ["PATH"] = root + os.pathsep + os.environ.get("PATH", "")
    dotnet = shutil.which("dotnet")
    if not dotnet:
        die(".NET SDK not found: run the tasks with mise (mise run setup installs it), or set DOTNET_ROOT")
    return dotnet


def godot_version(godot):
    proc = subprocess.run([str(godot), "--headless", "--version"], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True,
                          text=True, errors="replace", timeout=300)
    lines = [line.strip() for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    return lines[-1] if lines else ""


# --- Setup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def lfs_pointers():
    """The files the game is made from that are still Git LFS pointers (a clone made without Git LFS)."""
    pointers = []
    for path in [*MAC_RESOURCES.rglob("*"), REPO / MARVIN_STEP]:
        try:
            if path.is_file() and path.stat().st_size < 1024:
                with open(path, "rb") as f:
                    if f.read(len(LFS_POINTER)) == LFS_POINTER:
                        pointers.append(path)
        except OSError:
            pass
    return pointers


def fetch_lfs(pointers):
    say(f"Git LFS: fetching {len(pointers)} files (textures, mesh sources, Marvin's CAD master)")
    git = shutil.which("git") or die("git not found")
    if subprocess.run([git, "lfs", "version"], capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
        die("Git LFS not found: run the tasks with mise (it provides Git LFS), or install Git LFS")
    configured = subprocess.run([git, "config", "--get", "filter.lfs.process"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True,
                                text=True).stdout.strip()
    config, hooks = [], None
    if not configured:
        # This git has no Git LFS (Apple's git on a new Mac). Use mise's git-lfs for this command only and leave
        # .git/config and .git/hooks alone, so that git keeps working where git-lfs is not on PATH (Git LFS's hooks,
        # which `git lfs pull` would install, stop `git push` without it).
        hooks = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="marvin-lfs-hooks-")
        config = ["-c", "filter.lfs.clean=git-lfs clean -- %f", "-c", "filter.lfs.smudge=git-lfs smudge -- %f",
                  "-c", "filter.lfs.process=git-lfs filter-process", "-c", "filter.lfs.required=true",
                  "-c", f"core.hooksPath={hooks}"]
    try:
        run([git, *config, "lfs", "pull", f"--include={LFS_INCLUDE}"], cwd=REPO)
        if config:
            # Index the files once more through the LFS filter a moment later: git, without the filter, would take
            # files written in the same second as its index for changed ones.
            time.sleep(1.5)
            subprocess.run([git, *config, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no"], cwd=REPO,
                           capture_output=True)
    finally:
        if hooks:
            shutil.rmtree(hooks, ignore_errors=True)
    left = lfs_pointers()
    if left:
        die(f"Git LFS: {len(left)} files are still pointers, e.g. {left[0]}")
    if not configured:
        print("    (Your git has no Git LFS, so a later `git pull` leaves changed LFS files as pointers until the next "
              "`mise run setup`.)", flush=True)


def prepare_assets():
    env = dict(os.environ)
    if env.get("MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES"):
        say(f"Assets: from MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES={env['MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES']}")
    else:
        pointers = lfs_pointers()
        if pointers:
            fetch_lfs(pointers)
        else:
            say("Git LFS: files present")
        say("Assets: the robots' meshes (scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py, skipped when up to date)")
        run([sys.executable, REPO / "scripts" / "prepare-simulator-assets.py"], cwd=REPO)
        env["MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES"] = str(MAC_RESOURCES)  # this checkout's, also in a git worktree
    say("Assets: into assets/ (tools/sync-assets.py)")
    run([sys.executable, ROOT / "tools" / "sync-assets.py"], cwd=ROOT, env=env)


def build():
    say("Build: C# (MarvinGodot, MarvinCore)")
    run([setup_dotnet(), "build", ROOT / "MarvinGodot.csproj", "-nologo", "-v", "q"], cwd=ROOT)


def import_project(godot, log_name="import.log"):
    first = not (ROOT / ".godot" / "imported").is_dir()
    say("Godot: importing textures and audio" + (" (the first time takes a few minutes)" if first else ""))
    log = ROOT / "build" / log_name
    log.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with open(log, "wb") as f:
        proc = run([godot, "--headless", "--path", ROOT, "--import"], check=False, stdout=f, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        print(tail(log), file=sys.stderr)
        die(f"Godot import failed (exit {proc.returncode}), log: {log}")


def is_set_up():
    return (ROOT / "assets" / "Marvin" / "geometry.bin").is_file() and (ROOT / ".godot" / "imported").is_dir()


def cmd_setup(args):
    if args:
        die("setup takes no arguments")
    start = time.time()
    godot, dotnet = find_godot(), setup_dotnet()
    version = godot_version(godot)
    sdk = subprocess.run([dotnet, "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    print(f"    Godot  {version or '?'}  {godot}\n    .NET   {sdk or '?'}  {dotnet}\n"
          f"    Python {platform.python_version()}  {sys.executable}", flush=True)
    if not version.startswith(GODOT_VERSION):
        print(f"    warning: the port is made for Godot {GODOT_VERSION} (mise.toml)", flush=True)
    prepare_assets()
    build()
    import_project(godot)
    say(f"Ready ({time.time() - start:.0f} s). Play: mise run play")
    return 0


def ready():
    """Godot, after setting up what is missing and building the C# (the game runs the last build)."""
    if is_set_up():
        build()
    else:
        say("Not set up yet: running setup first")
        cmd_setup([])
    return find_godot()


# --- Play, test, checks ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def cmd_play(args):
    godot = ready()
    godot = dev_app(godot) if MACOS else godot
    # Flags are the game's (after "--", OS.GetCmdlineUserArgs); with a "--" of their own, Godot's come before it.
    args = args if not args or "--" in args else ["--", *args]
    return run([godot, "--path", ROOT, *args], check=False).returncode


DEV_APP = ROOT / "build" / "dev" / "Marvin Simulator.app"
DEV_APP_VERSION = "1"  # bump when dev_app changes what it makes


def dev_app(godot):
    """The editor binary in a copy of Godot's app named Marvin Simulator, so that the menu bar and the Dock show the
    game's name and icon (macOS takes them from the app's Info.plist, which Godot cannot change at run time; exports
    have their own). The copy is an APFS clone (no extra disk space) with a new Info.plist and icon, signed ad hoc.
    Remade when Godot or the icon changes; on any failure, play runs Godot's own app."""
    source = godot.parent.parent.parent
    if source.suffix != ".app" or source == DEV_APP:
        return godot
    icon = ROOT / "assets" / "Icons" / "AppIconLight.png"
    stamp_file = DEV_APP.parent / "dev-app.stamp"  # outside the signed bundle
    stamp = "\n".join([DEV_APP_VERSION, str(source), str((source / "Contents" / "Info.plist").stat().st_mtime_ns),
                       str(icon.stat().st_mtime_ns) if icon.is_file() else "-"])
    binary = DEV_APP / "Contents" / "MacOS" / godot.name
    if binary.is_file() and stamp_file.is_file() and stamp_file.read_text() == stamp:
        return binary
    say(f"Making {DEV_APP.relative_to(ROOT)} (Godot's app with the game's name and icon)")
    try:
        shutil.rmtree(DEV_APP, ignore_errors=True)
        DEV_APP.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        quiet = {"stdout": subprocess.DEVNULL, "stderr": subprocess.PIPE, "text": True}
        if subprocess.run(["cp", "-cR", source, DEV_APP], **quiet).returncode:  # clone; a copy off APFS
            shutil.copytree(source, DEV_APP, symlinks=True)
        plist = DEV_APP / "Contents" / "Info.plist"
        steps = [["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleName", "-string", "Marvin Simulator", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleDisplayName", "-string", "Marvin Simulator", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleIdentifier", "-string", "io.entire.marvin.simulator.godot.dev", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-remove", "CFBundleDocumentTypes", plist]]
        if icon.is_file():
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
                iconset = Path(tmp) / "Marvin.iconset"
                iconset.mkdir()
                for size in (16, 32, 128, 256, 512):
                    for scale in (1, 2):
                        name = f"icon_{size}x{size}{'@2x' if scale == 2 else ''}.png"
                        run(["sips", "-z", size * scale, size * scale, icon, "--out", iconset / name], **quiet)
                run(["iconutil", "-c", "icns", iconset, "-o", DEV_APP / "Contents" / "Resources" / "Marvin.icns"],
                    **quiet)
            # The asset catalog's icon (CFBundleIconName) takes precedence over CFBundleIconFile.
            steps += [["plutil", "-remove", "CFBundleIconName", plist],
                      ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleIconFile", "-string", "Marvin.icns", plist]]
        for step in steps:
            subprocess.run(step, **quiet)  # -remove of a missing key fails harmlessly
        subprocess.run(["xattr", "-dr", "com.apple.quarantine", DEV_APP], **quiet)
        # Only the outer bundle changed: re-sign it ad hoc, keeping Godot's entitlements and hardened runtime.
        signed = subprocess.run(["codesign", "--force", "--sign", "-", "--preserve-metadata=entitlements,flags",
                                 DEV_APP], **quiet)
        if signed.returncode:
            raise OSError(signed.stderr.strip())
        stamp_file.write_text(stamp)
        return binary
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError, SystemExit) as error:
        print(f"    warning: {error or 'failed'}; playing in Godot's own app", flush=True)
        shutil.rmtree(DEV_APP, ignore_errors=True)
        return godot


def cmd_godot(args):
    setup_dotnet()
    return run([find_godot(), "--path", ROOT, *args], check=False).returncode


def cmd_build(args):
    build()
    return 0


def cmd_test(args):
    if len(args) > 1 or (args and args[0].startswith("-")):
        die("test takes one argument: comma-separated modes of tools/ci/headless-modes.py, or all")
    modes = args[0] if args else SMOKE_MODES
    godot = ready()
    say(f"Smoke test, headless: {'every mode' if modes == 'all' else modes}")
    cmd = [sys.executable, ROOT / "tools" / "ci" / "headless-modes.py", "--godot", godot, "--out", ROOT / "build" / "test",
           "--title", "Quick smoke test (headless) against Godot on macOS"]
    return run(cmd + ([] if modes == "all" else ["--only", modes]), check=False, cwd=ROOT).returncode


def cmd_checks(args):
    dotnet = setup_dotnet()
    return run([dotnet, "run", "--project", ROOT / "src" / "Checks" / "MarvinChecks.csproj", "-c", "Release", "-nologo",
                "--", *args], check=False, cwd=ROOT).returncode


# --- Export ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class RangeReader(io.RawIOBase):
    """A remote file read with HTTP range requests, so that zipfile downloads only the members it extracts."""

    def __init__(self, url):
        self.url, self.pos = url, 0
        with self._get(0, 0) as response:
            if response.status != 206:
                raise OSError(f"HTTP {response.status} to a range request")
            self.size = int(response.headers["Content-Range"].rsplit("/", 1)[1])

    def _get(self, first, last):
        request = urllib.request.Request(self.url, headers={"Range": f"bytes={first}-{last}",
                                                            "User-Agent": "marvin-simulator-godot"})
        return urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60)

    def readable(self):
        return True

    def seekable(self):
        return True

    def tell(self):
        return self.pos

    def seek(self, offset, whence=io.SEEK_SET):
        self.pos = {io.SEEK_SET: 0, io.SEEK_CUR: self.pos, io.SEEK_END: self.size}[whence] + offset
        return self.pos

    def readinto(self, buffer):
        end = min(self.pos + len(buffer), self.size)
        if end <= self.pos:
            return 0
        for attempt in range(5):
            try:
                with self._get(self.pos, end - 1) as response:
                    if response.status != 206:
                        raise OSError(f"HTTP {response.status} to a range request")
                    data = response.read()
                break
            except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException):
                if attempt == 4:
                    raise
                time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
        buffer[:len(data)] = data
        self.pos += len(data)
        return len(data)


def templates_folder(template_version):
    if MACOS:
        base = Path.home() / "Library" / "Application Support" / "Godot"
    elif WINDOWS:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("APPDATA") or Path.home() / "AppData" / "Roaming") / "Godot"
    else:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME") or Path.home() / ".local" / "share") / "godot"
    return base / "export_templates" / template_version


def ensure_templates(folder, template_version, needed):
    """Fetches the export template files the presets need from Godot's release archive (1.2 GB for every platform;
    only the needed members, about 200 MB for both presets, are downloaded)."""
    missing = [name for name in ["icudt_godot.dat", *needed, "version.txt"] if not (folder / name).is_file()]
    if not missing:
        return
    match = re.match(r"(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\.([a-z0-9]+)\.mono$", template_version)
    if not match:
        die(f"unexpected Godot version {template_version}")
    tag = f"{match[1]}-{match[2]}"
    url = f"https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/{tag}/Godot_v{tag}_mono_export_templates.tpz"
    say(f"Export templates {template_version}: fetching {', '.join(missing)} into {folder}")
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    whole = None
    try:
        source = io.BufferedReader(RangeReader(url), buffer_size=8 << 20)
    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:
        print(f"    no range requests ({error}): downloading the whole archive", flush=True)
        fd, whole = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".tpz")
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as f, urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as response:
            shutil.copyfileobj(response, f, 1 << 20)
        source = open(whole, "rb")
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(source) as archive:
            for name in missing:  # version.txt last: Godot takes the folder for complete once it is there
                info = archive.getinfo(f"templates/{name}")
                print(f"    {name} ({info.file_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)", flush=True)
                partial = folder / f"{name}.part"
                with archive.open(info) as src, open(partial, "wb") as dst:  # zipfile checks the CRC
                    shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst, 1 << 20)
                os.replace(partial, folder / name)
    finally:
        source.close()
        if whole:
            os.unlink(whole)


EXPORT_HELP = """mise run export [-- macos|windows] [--zip] [--debug]   (python tools/dev.py export ...)
  Release builds: build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app, build/windows/MarvinSimulator.exe (default: both on a Mac,
  windows elsewhere), checked by tools/export-verify.py. --zip also packs build/MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64.zip to
  copy to a PC; --debug uses the debug engine template (same C#, ExportDebug). Fetches the Godot export templates when
  they are missing."""


def cmd_export(args):
    platforms, mode, pack = [], "release", False
    for arg in args:
        if arg in PRESETS:
            platforms.append(arg)
        elif arg == "--debug":
            mode = "debug"
        elif arg == "--zip":
            pack = True
        elif arg in ("-h", "--help"):
            print(EXPORT_HELP)
            return 0
        else:
            die(f"export: unknown argument {arg}\n{EXPORT_HELP}")
    platforms = platforms or (["macos", "windows"] if MACOS else ["windows"])
    if not (ROOT / "assets" / "Marvin" / "geometry.bin").is_file():
        die("assets/ is missing: run mise run setup first")
    setup_dotnet()
    godot = find_godot()
    version = godot_version(godot)
    match = re.match(r"(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?\.[a-z0-9]+\.mono)", version)
    if not match:
        die(f"{godot} is not a Godot .NET editor (version {version!r})")
    folder = templates_folder(match[1])
    ensure_templates(folder, match[1], sorted({n for p in platforms for n in TEMPLATES[(p, mode)]}))

    # Imports first: the export packs the imported textures and the raw .wav files (importer "keep", sync-assets.py).
    import_project(godot)
    status = 0
    for name in platforms:
        preset, out = PRESETS[name]
        folder_out = (ROOT / out).parent
        shutil.rmtree(folder_out, ignore_errors=True)
        folder_out.mkdir(parents=True)
        log = ROOT / "build" / f"export-{name}.log"
        say(f"Exporting {preset} ({mode}) -> {out}")
        with open(log, "wb") as f:
            proc = run([godot, "--headless", "--path", ROOT, f"--export-{mode}", preset, ROOT / out], check=False,
                       stdout=f, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            print(tail(log), file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"dev.py: {preset} export failed, log: {log}", file=sys.stderr)
            status = 1
            continue
        errors = [line for line in log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
                  if re.search(r"(^|m)(ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR):", line)]
        if errors:
            print("\n".join(errors), file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"dev.py: {preset} export logged errors, log: {log}", file=sys.stderr)
            status = 1
        if run([sys.executable, ROOT / "tools" / "export-verify.py", folder_out], check=False, cwd=ROOT).returncode:
            status = 1
        if pack and name == "windows":
            archive = ROOT / "build" / "MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64"
            Path(f"{archive}.zip").unlink(missing_ok=True)
            shutil.make_archive(str(archive), "zip", folder_out)
            print("Packed build/MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64.zip", flush=True)
    return status


TASKS = {"setup": cmd_setup, "play": cmd_play, "test": cmd_test, "checks": cmd_checks, "export": cmd_export,
         "build": cmd_build, "godot": cmd_godot}


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2 or sys.argv[1] not in TASKS:
        print(__doc__.strip())
        return 0 if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help") else 2
    return TASKS[sys.argv[1]](sys.argv[2:])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
