# The Godot port's developer setup (apps/simulator-godot/mise.toml; README.md, "Setup") on fresh GitHub-hosted runners.
# Only mise is installed (jdx/mise-action without tools or cache); then exactly the documented commands: git clone,
# cd apps/simulator-godot, mise trust, mise run setup, mise run play (headless here: a game mode that quits by itself),
# and the quick headless smoke test (mise run test). Then: setup again (idempotent, seconds), the tasks leave the
# working tree as it was, and a release export of the runner's platform (the export templates fetched by the task).
name: Godot port setup with mise

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [codex/mos-aster-racing-city]
    paths:
      - apps/simulator-godot/mise.toml
      - apps/simulator-godot/tools/dev.py
      - apps/simulator-godot/tools/env.sh
      - apps/simulator-godot/tools/sync-assets.py
      - apps/simulator-godot/tools/export-verify.py
      - apps/simulator-godot/tools/ci/headless-modes.py
      - apps/simulator-godot/**/*.csproj
      - scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py
      - .github/workflows/godot-setup.yml

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: godot-setup-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  setup:
    name: mise run setup, play, test (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            export: windows
          - os: macos-latest
            export: macos
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            export: ''
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      # mise fetches Godot, Python and Git LFS from GitHub releases; the token avoids the shared runners' API limit.
      MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
        with:
          install: false  # the tasks install the tools, as on a developer's machine
          cache: false    # every run starts without them
      - name: git clone (this commit)
        run: |
          git clone --branch "${{ github.ref_name }}" "https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git" marvin
          git -C marvin checkout --detach "${{ github.sha }}"
      - name: mise trust
        working-directory: marvin/apps/simulator-godot
        run: mise trust
      - name: mise run setup
        working-directory: marvin/apps/simulator-godot
        run: mise run setup
      - name: mise run play (headless, --town-statistics)
        working-directory: marvin/apps/simulator-godot
        run: mise run play -- --headless --audio-driver Dummy -- --town-statistics "${{ runner.temp }}/play"
      - name: mise run test
        working-directory: marvin/apps/simulator-godot
        run: mise run test
      - name: mise run setup (again; nothing to do)
        working-directory: marvin/apps/simulator-godot
        run: mise run setup
      - name: The tasks left the working tree as it was
        working-directory: marvin
        run: |
          git status --short
          git diff --exit-code --stat
      - name: mise run export -- ${{ matrix.export }}
        if: ${{ matrix.export != '' }}
        working-directory: marvin/apps/simulator-godot
        run: mise run export -- ${{ matrix.export }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: setup-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: |
            marvin/apps/simulator-godot/build/test
            marvin/apps/simulator-godot/build/*.log
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: ignore
# The Godot port (apps/simulator-godot) on a GitHub-hosted Windows runner, which has no GPU.
# What it answers, in the job summaries and the uploaded artifacts (apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md,
# "Release builds and Windows", explains the tooling in apps/simulator-godot/tools/ci):
#   checks  - the C# SimulationChecks against the Swift reference, default and with MARVIN_PORTABLE_MATH=1
#             (a numeric difference is a finding, a crash or failed check fails the job), on Windows, Linux and macOS;
#   libm    - which C library functions round differently from Darwin's, call by call (tools/checks --libm-probe);
#   assets  - the game's assets generated on Windows with the repository's exporters, against a Mac's;
#   game    - the generated town (--town-statistics against the macOS game, --town-reference-dump against Godot on
#             macOS), the deterministic logic modes headless against Godot on macOS and the macOS game, then the
#             Windows export (tools/export windows) and the exported exe headless (a crash, also one while quitting
#             after every report was written, fails the job), and diagnostics;
#   render  - Direct3D 12 (WARP) and Vulkan through Mesa's lavapipe, a few deterministic captures against
#             Godot-on-macOS captures (a driver that does not render is not a failure, a crash is).
# On demand (workflow_dispatch, exit_diagnostics): how the builds end, repeated runs and cdb with full page heap and SOS
# (tools/ci/exit-diagnostics.ps1), in the game and render jobs.
name: Godot port on Windows

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      regenerate_assets:
        description: Generate the game's assets again instead of restoring them from the cache
        type: boolean
        default: false
      exit_diagnostics:
        description: How the builds end (tools/ci/exit-diagnostics.ps1) - repeated runs, cdb with full page heap and SOS
        type: boolean
        default: false
  push:
    branches: [codex/mos-aster-racing-city]
    paths:
      - apps/simulator-godot/**
      - apps/simulator-macos/Resources/**
      - scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py
      - scripts/export-marvin-simulator.py
      - scripts/export-r2d2-simulator.py
      - scripts/export-racers-simulator.py
      - scripts/racer_gltf.py
      - hardware/mechanical/step/marvin_robot.step
      - .github/workflows/godot-windows.yml

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: godot-windows-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  GODOT_VERSION: '4.7.2'
  MESA_VERSION: '26.2.4'          # pal1000/mesa-dist-win, for lavapipe
  DOTNET_VERSION: '8.0.x'
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: '1'
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: '1'
  PYTHONUTF8: '1'
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: '1'

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  checks:
    # Windows is the question; Linux (glibc) and a macOS runner (Darwin libm, where the reference comes from) show
    # whether a difference is Windows' C runtime or any libm other than Darwin's.
    name: Core maths (SimulationChecks, ${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [windows-latest, ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: ${{ env.DOTNET_VERSION }}
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.nuget/packages
          key: nuget-checks-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('apps/simulator-godot/src/**/*.csproj') }}
      - name: Build
        working-directory: apps/simulator-godot
        run: dotnet build src/Checks/MarvinChecks.csproj -c Release -nologo -v q
      - name: Run SimulationChecks (default, then MARVIN_PORTABLE_MATH=1)
        id: run
        working-directory: apps/simulator-godot
        run: |
          mkdir -p ../../out/checks
          set +e
          dotnet run --project src/Checks/MarvinChecks.csproj -c Release --no-build > ../../out/checks/checks-default.txt 2> ../../out/checks/checks-default.err
          echo "default=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          MARVIN_PORTABLE_MATH=1 dotnet run --project src/Checks/MarvinChecks.csproj -c Release --no-build > ../../out/checks/checks-portable.txt 2> ../../out/checks/checks-portable.err
          echo "portable=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          cat ../../out/checks/checks-default.err ../../out/checks/checks-portable.err
          exit 0
      - name: Compare with the Swift reference
        run: >-
          python apps/simulator-godot/tools/ci/checks-report.py
          --reference apps/simulator-godot/src/Checks/reference/simulation-checks-swift.txt
          --run "default|out/checks/checks-default.txt|${{ steps.run.outputs.default }}"
          --run "MARVIN_PORTABLE_MATH=1|out/checks/checks-portable.txt|${{ steps.run.outputs.portable }}"
          --out out/checks --title "Core maths on ${{ runner.os }} (${{ matrix.os }}): SimulationChecks against the Swift reference"
      - name: Portable maths against Darwin and NEON (macOS runner; tools/checks --portable-math)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && runner.os == 'macOS' }}
        working-directory: apps/simulator-godot
        run: |
          # The software NEON rsqrt/recip that x64 uses, for all 2^32 floats, and 4 million hypot pairs against libSystem.
          dotnet run --project src/Checks/MarvinChecks.csproj -c Release --no-build -- --portable-math 4 | tee ../../out/checks/portable-math.txt
          {
            echo "## Portable maths on the macOS runner (arm64)"
            echo
            echo '```'
            cat ../../out/checks/portable-math.txt
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: libm probe (the platform's sin, cos, atan2, exp, pow ... for the game's arguments)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        working-directory: apps/simulator-godot
        run: dotnet run --project src/Checks/MarvinChecks.csproj -c Release --no-build -- --libm-probe ../../out/libm
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: checks-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: out/checks
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        with:
          name: libm-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: out/libm
          retention-days: 7

  libm:
    name: Which libm functions differ from macOS
    needs: checks
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: libm-*
          path: probes
      - name: Compare Windows and Linux with macOS, call by call
        run: >-
          python3 apps/simulator-godot/tools/ci/libm-report.py --reference "macOS|probes/libm-macos-latest"
          --run "Windows|probes/libm-windows-latest" --run "Linux|probes/libm-ubuntu-latest" --out out/libm
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: libm-report
          path: out/libm
          retention-days: 14

  assets:
    name: Game assets (generated on Windows)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Cache key (exporters, their LFS sources by object id, the macOS Resources, the sync script)
        id: key
        run: |
          key=$(git ls-files -s apps/simulator-macos/Resources hardware/mechanical/step/marvin_robot.step \
                scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py scripts/export-marvin-simulator.py scripts/export-r2d2-simulator.py \
                scripts/export-racers-simulator.py scripts/racer_gltf.py apps/simulator-godot/tools/sync-assets.py \
                | sha256sum | cut -c1-20)
          echo "key=$key" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Restore the generated assets
        id: cache
        if: ${{ !inputs.regenerate_assets }}
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: apps/simulator-godot/assets
          key: godot-assets-windows-${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
      - name: Fetch the LFS sources (macOS Resources, Marvin's STEP master)
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: git lfs pull --include="apps/simulator-macos/Resources/**,hardware/mechanical/step/marvin_robot.step"
      - name: Generate (scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py, as build-app.sh does)
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: python scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py
      - name: Sync (apps/simulator-godot/tools/sync-assets.py)
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: python apps/simulator-godot/tools/sync-assets.py
      - name: Save the generated assets
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: apps/simulator-godot/assets
          key: godot-assets-windows-${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
      - name: Compare with a Mac's assets
        run: python apps/simulator-godot/tools/ci/assets-report.py --out out/assets
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: godot-assets
          path: apps/simulator-godot/assets
          retention-days: 3
          compression-level: 1
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: assets-report
          path: out/assets
          retention-days: 14

  game:
    name: Town, headless modes, export
    needs: assets
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 120
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

def say(message):
    print(f"==> {message}", flush=True)


def die(message):
    print(f"dev.py: {message}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    sys.exit(1)


def run(cmd, check=True, **kwargs):
    cmd = [str(c) for c in cmd]
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, **kwargs)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        sys.exit(130)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        die(f"{' '.join([Path(cmd[0]).name, *cmd[1:3]])} ... failed (exit {proc.returncode})")
    return proc


def tail(path, lines=40):
    return "\n".join(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()[-lines:])

def mise_where(tool):
    """The install folder of a tool that mise.toml pins, or None (no mise, config not trusted, tool not installed)."""
    mise = shutil.which("mise")
    if not mise:
        return None
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run([mise, "where", tool], cwd=ROOT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True,
                              text=True, timeout=120)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    lines = proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()
    folder = Path(lines[-1].strip()) if proc.returncode == 0 and lines else None
    return folder if folder and folder.is_dir() else None


def godot_in(folder):
    """The Godot .NET editor binary in an unpacked release (on Windows the console variant, which prints the log)."""
    if MACOS:
        candidates = [folder / "Godot_mono.app" / "Contents" / "MacOS" / "Godot"]
    else:
        pattern = "Godot_v*_mono_*_console.exe" if WINDOWS else "Godot_v*_mono_linux*"
        candidates = [c for c in sorted(folder.glob(pattern)) + sorted(folder.glob(f"*/{pattern}"))
                      if WINDOWS or re.search(r"\.(x86_64|arm64)$", c.name)]
    return next((c for c in candidates if c.is_file()), None)


def find_godot():
    if os.environ.get("GODOT"):
        godot = Path(os.environ["GODOT"])
        if not godot.is_file():
            die(f"GODOT is set to {godot}, which does not exist")
        return godot
    folder = mise_where("godot-mono")
    godot = godot_in(folder) if folder else None
    for apps in ([Path.home() / "Applications", Path("/Applications")] if MACOS and not godot else []):
        godot = godot or godot_in(apps)
    if not godot:
        die("Godot 4.7.2 .NET not found: run the tasks with mise (mise run setup installs it), "
            "or set GODOT to the editor binary (README.md)")
    return godot


def setup_dotnet():
    """Puts the .NET SDK on PATH and in DOTNET_ROOT, for dotnet and for Godot, which loads .NET from there."""
    root = os.environ.get("DOTNET_ROOT")
    if not root:
        for folder in (mise_where("dotnet"), Path.home() / ".dotnet"):
            if folder and (folder / f"dotnet{EXE}").is_file():
                root = str(folder)
                break
    if root:
        os.environ["DOTNET_ROOT"] = root
        paths = [os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(p)) for p in os.environ.get("PATH", "").split(os.pathsep) if p]
        if os.path.normcase(os.path.normpath(root)) not in paths:
            os.environ["PATH"] = root + os.pathsep + os.environ.get("PATH", "")
    dotnet = shutil.which("dotnet")
    if not dotnet:
        die(".NET SDK not found: run the tasks with mise (mise run setup installs it), or set DOTNET_ROOT")
    return dotnet


def godot_version(godot):
    proc = subprocess.run([str(godot), "--headless", "--version"], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True,
                          text=True, errors="replace", timeout=300)
    lines = [line.strip() for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    return lines[-1] if lines else ""

def lfs_pointers():
    """The files the game is made from that are still Git LFS pointers (a clone made without Git LFS)."""
    pointers = []
    for path in [*MAC_RESOURCES.rglob("*"), REPO / MARVIN_STEP]:
        try:
            if path.is_file() and path.stat().st_size < 1024:
                with open(path, "rb") as f:
                    if f.read(len(LFS_POINTER)) == LFS_POINTER:
                        pointers.append(path)
        except OSError:
            pass
    return pointers


def fetch_lfs(pointers):
    say(f"Git LFS: fetching {len(pointers)} files (textures, mesh sources, Marvin's CAD master)")
    git = shutil.which("git") or die("git not found")
    if subprocess.run([git, "lfs", "version"], capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
        die("Git LFS not found: run the tasks with mise (it provides Git LFS), or install Git LFS")
    configured = subprocess.run([git, "config", "--get", "filter.lfs.process"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True,
                                text=True).stdout.strip()
    config, hooks = [], None
    if not configured:
        # This git has no Git LFS (Apple's git on a new Mac). Use mise's git-lfs for this command only and leave
        # .git/config and .git/hooks alone, so that git keeps working where git-lfs is not on PATH (Git LFS's hooks,
        # which `git lfs pull` would install, stop `git push` without it).
        hooks = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="marvin-lfs-hooks-")
        config = ["-c", "filter.lfs.clean=git-lfs clean -- %f", "-c", "filter.lfs.smudge=git-lfs smudge -- %f",
                  "-c", "filter.lfs.process=git-lfs filter-process", "-c", "filter.lfs.required=true",
                  "-c", f"core.hooksPath={hooks}"]
    try:
        run([git, *config, "lfs", "pull", f"--include={LFS_INCLUDE}"], cwd=REPO)
        if config:
            # Index the files once more through the LFS filter a moment later: git, without the filter, would take
            # files written in the same second as its index for changed ones.
            time.sleep(1.5)
            subprocess.run([git, *config, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no"], cwd=REPO,
                           capture_output=True)
    finally:
        if hooks:
            shutil.rmtree(hooks, ignore_errors=True)
    left = lfs_pointers()
    if left:
        die(f"Git LFS: {len(left)} files are still pointers, e.g. {left[0]}")
    if not configured:
        print("    (Your git has no Git LFS, so a later `git pull` leaves changed LFS files as pointers until the next "
              "`mise run setup`.)", flush=True)

      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: ${{ env.DOTNET_VERSION }}
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.nuget/packages
          key: nuget-checks-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('apps/simulator-godot/src/**/*.csproj') }}
      - name: Build
        working-directory: apps/simulator-godot
        run: dotnet build src/Checks/MarvinChecks.csproj -c Release -nologo -v q
      - name: Run SimulationChecks (default, then MARVIN_PORTABLE_MATH=1)
        id: run
        working-directory: apps/simulator-godot
        run: |
          mkdir -p ../../out/checks
          set +e
          dotnet run --project src/Checks/MarvinChecks.csproj -c Release --no-build > ../../out/checks/checks-default.txt 2> ../../out/checks/checks-default.err
          echo "default=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          MARVIN_PORTABLE_MATH=1 dotnet run --project src/Checks/MarvinChecks.csproj -c Release --no-build > ../../out/checks/checks-portable.txt 2> ../../out/checks/checks-portable.err
          echo "portable=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          cat ../../out/checks/checks-default.err ../../out/checks/checks-portable.err
          exit 0
      - name: Compare with the Swift reference
        run: >-
          python apps/simulator-godot/tools/ci/checks-report.py
          --reference apps/simulator-godot/src/Checks/reference/simulation-checks-swift.txt
          --run "default|out/checks/checks-default.txt|${{ steps.run.outputs.default }}"
          --run "MARVIN_PORTABLE_MATH=1|out/checks/checks-portable.txt|${{ steps.run.outputs.portable }}"
          --out out/checks --title "Core maths on ${{ runner.os }} (${{ matrix.os }}): SimulationChecks against the Swift reference"
      - name: Portable maths against Darwin and NEON (macOS runner; tools/checks --portable-math)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && runner.os == 'macOS' }}
        working-directory: apps/simulator-godot
        run: |
          # The software NEON rsqrt/recip that x64 uses, for all 2^32 floats, and 4 million hypot pairs against libSystem.
          dotnet run --project src/Checks/MarvinChecks.csproj -c Release --no-build -- --portable-math 4 | tee ../../out/checks/portable-math.txt
          {
            echo "## Portable maths on the macOS runner (arm64)"
            echo
            echo '```'
            cat ../../out/checks/portable-math.txt
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: libm probe (the platform's sin, cos, atan2, exp, pow ... for the game's arguments)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        working-directory: apps/simulator-godot
        run: dotnet run --project src/Checks/MarvinChecks.csproj -c Release --no-build -- --libm-probe ../../out/libm
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: checks-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: out/checks
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        with:
          name: libm-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: out/libm
          retention-days: 7

  libm:
    name: Which libm functions differ from macOS
    needs: checks
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: libm-*
          path: probes
      - name: Compare Windows and Linux with macOS, call by call
        run: >-
          python3 apps/simulator-godot/tools/ci/libm-report.py --reference "macOS|probes/libm-macos-latest"
          --run "Windows|probes/libm-windows-latest" --run "Linux|probes/libm-ubuntu-latest" --out out/libm
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4

          path: out/libm

  assets:
    name: Game assets (generated on Windows)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Cache key (exporters, their LFS sources by object id, the macOS Resources, the sync script)
        id: key
        run: |
          key=$(git ls-files -s apps/simulator-macos/Resources hardware/mechanical/step/marvin_robot.step \
                scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py scripts/export-marvin-simulator.py scripts/export-r2d2-simulator.py \

      - name: Restore the generated assets
        id: cache
        if: ${{ !inputs.regenerate_assets }}
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: apps/simulator-godot/assets
          key: godot-assets-windows-${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
      - name: Fetch the LFS sources (macOS Resources, Marvin's STEP master)
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'

      - name: Generate (scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py, as build-app.sh does)

      - name: Save the generated assets

        with:

        if: always()
        with:

          path: out/assets

    name: Town, headless modes, export
    needs: assets

game's name and icon (macOS takes them from the app's Info.plist, which Godot cannot change at run time; exports
    have their own). The copy is an APFS clone (no extra disk space) with a new Info.plist and icon, signed ad hoc.
    Remade when Godot or the icon changes; on any failure, play runs Godot's own app."""
    source = godot.parent.parent.parent
    if source.suffix != ".app" or source == DEV_APP:
        return godot
    icon = ROOT / "assets" / "Icons" / "AppIconLight.png"
    stamp_file = DEV_APP.parent / "dev-app.stamp"  # outside the signed bundle
    stamp = "\n".join([DEV_APP_VERSION, str(source), str((source / "Contents" / "Info.plist").stat().st_mtime_ns),
                       str(icon.stat().st_mtime_ns) if icon.is_file() else "-"])
    binary = DEV_APP / "Contents" / "MacOS" / godot.name
    if binary.is_file() and stamp_file.is_file() and stamp_file.read_text() == stamp:
        return binary
    say(f"Making {DEV_APP.relative_to(ROOT)} (Godot's app with the game's name and icon)")
    try:
        shutil.rmtree(DEV_APP, ignore_errors=True)
        DEV_APP.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        quiet = {"stdout": subprocess.DEVNULL, "stderr": subprocess.PIPE, "text": True}
        if subprocess.run(["cp", "-cR", source, DEV_APP], **quiet).returncode:  # clone; a copy off APFS
            shutil.copytree(source, DEV_APP, symlinks=True)
        plist = DEV_APP / "Contents" / "Info.plist"
        steps = [["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleName", "-string", "Marvin Simulator", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleDisplayName", "-string", "Marvin Simulator", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleIdentifier", "-string", "io.entire.marvin.simulator.godot.dev", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-remove", "CFBundleDocumentTypes", plist]]
        if icon.is_file():
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
                iconset = Path(tmp) / "Marvin.iconset"
                iconset.mkdir()
                for size in (16, 32, 128, 256, 512):
                    for scale in (1, 2):
                        name = f"icon_{size}x{size}{'@2x' if scale == 2 else ''}.png"
                        run(["sips", "-z", size * scale, size * scale, icon, "--out", iconset / name], **quiet)
                run(["iconutil", "-c", "icns", iconset, "-o", DEV_APP / "Contents" / "Resources" / "Marvin.icns"],
                    **quiet)
            # The asset catalog's icon (CFBundleIconName) takes precedence over CFBundleIconFile.
            steps += [["plutil", "-remove", "CFBundleIconName", plist],
                      ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleIconFile", "-string", "Marvin.icns", plist]]
        for step in steps:
            subprocess.run(step, **quiet)  # -remove of a missing key fails harmlessly
        subprocess.run(["xattr", "-dr", "com.apple.quarantine", DEV_APP], **quiet)
        # Only the outer bundle changed: re-sign it ad hoc, keeping Godot's entitlements and hardened runtime.
        signed = subprocess.run(["codesign", "--force", "--sign", "-", "--preserve-metadata=entitlements,flags",
                                 DEV_APP], **quiet)
        if signed.returncode:
            raise OSError(signed.stderr.strip())
        stamp_file.write_text(stamp)
        return binary
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError, SystemExit) as error:
        print(f"    warning: {error or 'failed'}; playing in Godot's own app", flush=True)
        shutil.rmtree(DEV_APP, ignore_errors=True)
        return godot

# --- Export ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class RangeReader(io.RawIOBase):
    """A remote file read with HTTP range requests, so that zipfile downloads only the members it extracts."""

    def __init__(self, url):
        self.url, self.pos = url, 0
        with self._get(0, 0) as response:
            if response.status != 206:
                raise OSError(f"HTTP {response.status} to a range request")
            self.size = int(response.headers["Content-Range"].rsplit("/", 1)[1])

    def _get(self, first, last):
        request = urllib.request.Request(self.url, headers={"Range": f"bytes={first}-{last}",
                                                            "User-Agent": "marvin-simulator-godot"})
        return urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60)

    def readable(self):
        return True

    def seekable(self):
        return True

    def tell(self):
        return self.pos

    def seek(self, offset, whence=io.SEEK_SET):
        self.pos = {io.SEEK_SET: 0, io.SEEK_CUR: self.pos, io.SEEK_END: self.size}[whence] + offset
        return self.pos

    def readinto(self, buffer):
        end = min(self.pos + len(buffer), self.size)
        if end <= self.pos:
            return 0
        for attempt in range(5):
            try:
                with self._get(self.pos, end - 1) as response:
                    if response.status != 206:
                        raise OSError(f"HTTP {response.status} to a range request")
                    data = response.read()
                break
            except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException):
                if attempt == 4:
                    raise
                time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
        buffer[:len(data)] = data
        self.pos += len(data)
        return len(data)


def templates_folder(template_version):
    if MACOS:
        base = Path.home() / "Library" / "Application Support" / "Godot"
    elif WINDOWS:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("APPDATA") or Path.home() / "AppData" / "Roaming") / "Godot"
    else:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME") or Path.home() / ".local" / "share") / "godot"
    return base / "export_templates" / template_version


def ensure_templates(folder, template_version, needed):
    """Fetches the export template files the presets need from Godot's release archive (1.2 GB for every platform;
    only the needed members, about 200 MB for both presets, are downloaded)."""
    missing = [name for name in ["icudt_godot.dat", *needed, "version.txt"] if not (folder / name).is_file()]
    if not missing:
        return
    match = re.match(r"(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\.([a-z0-9]+)\.mono$", template_version)
    if not match:
        die(f"unexpected Godot version {template_version}")
    tag = f"{match[1]}-{match[2]}"
    url = f"https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/{tag}/Godot_v{tag}_mono_export_templates.tpz"
    say(f"Export templates {template_version}: fetching {', '.join(missing)} into {folder}")
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    whole = None
    try:
        source = io.BufferedReader(RangeReader(url), buffer_size=8 << 20)
    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:
        print(f"    no range requests ({error}): downloading the whole archive", flush=True)
        fd, whole = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".tpz")
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as f, urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as response:
            shutil.copyfileobj(response, f, 1 << 20)
        source = open(whole, "rb")
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(source) as archive:
            for name in missing:  # version.txt last: Godot takes the folder for complete once it is there
                info = archive.getinfo(f"templates/{name}")
                print(f"    {name} ({info.file_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)", flush=True)
                partial = folder / f"{name}.part"
                with archive.open(info) as src, open(partial, "wb") as dst:  # zipfile checks the CRC
                    shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst, 1 << 20)
                os.replace(partial, folder / name)
    finally:
        source.close()
        if whole:
            os.unlink(whole)


EXPORT_HELP = """mise run export [-- macos|windows] [--zip] [--debug]   (python tools/dev.py export ...)
  Release builds: build/macos/Marvin Simulator.app, build/windows/MarvinSimulator.exe (default: both on a Mac,
  windows elsewhere), checked by tools/export-verify.py. --zip also packs build/MarvinSimulator-windows-x86_64.zip to
  copy to a PC; --debug uses the debug engine template (same C#, ExportDebug). Fetches the Godot export templates when
  they are missing."""


def cmd_export(args):
    platforms, mode, pack = [], "release", False
    for arg in args:
        if arg in PRESETS:
            platforms.append(arg)
        elif arg == "--debug":
            mode = "debug"
        elif arg == "--zip":
            pack = True
        elif arg in ("-h", "--help"):
            print(EXPORT_HELP)
            return 0
        else:
            die(f"export: unknown argument {arg}\n{EXPORT_HELP}")
    platforms = platforms or (["macos", "windows"] if MACOS else ["windows"])
    if not (ROOT / "assets" / "Marvin" / "geometry.bin").is_file():
        die("assets/ is missing: run mise run setup first")
    setup_dotnet()

class RangeReader(io.RawIOBase):
    """A remote file read with HTTP range requests, so that zipfile downloads only the members it extracts."""

    def __init__(self, url):
        self.url, self.pos = url, 0
        with self._get(0, 0) as response:
            if response.status != 206:
                raise OSError(f"HTTP {response.status} to a range request")
            self.size = int(response.headers["Content-Range"].rsplit("/", 1)[1])

    def _get(self, first, last):
        request = urllib.request.Request(self.url, headers={"Range": f"bytes={first}-{last}",
                                                            "User-Agent": "marvin-simulator-godot"})
        return urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60)

    def readable(self):
        return True

    def seekable(self):
        return True

    def tell(self):
        return self.pos

    def seek(self, offset, whence=io.SEEK_SET):
        self.pos = {io.SEEK_SET: 0, io.SEEK_CUR: self.pos, io.SEEK_END: self.size}[whence] + offset
        return self.pos

    def readinto(self, buffer):
        end = min(self.pos + len(buffer), self.size)
        if end <= self.pos:
            return 0
        for attempt in range(5):
            try:
                with self._get(self.pos, end - 1) as response:
                    if response.status != 206:
                        raise OSError(f"HTTP {response.status} to a range request")
                    data = response.read()
                break
            except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException):
                if attempt == 4:
                    raise
                time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
        buffer[:len(data)] = data
        self.pos += len(data)
        return len(data)


def templates_folder(template_version):
    if MACOS:
        base = Path.home() / "Library" / "Application Support" / "Godot"
    elif WINDOWS:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("APPDATA") or Path.home() / "AppData" / "Roaming") / "Godot"
    else:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME") or Path.home() / ".local" / "share") / "godot"
    return base / "export_templates" / template_version


def ensure_templates(folder, template_version, needed):
    """Fetches the export template files the presets need from Godot's release archive (1.2 GB for every platform;
    only the needed members, about 200 MB for both presets, are downloaded)."""
    missing = [name for name in ["icudt_godot.dat", *needed, "version.txt"] if not (folder / name).is_file()]
    if not missing:
        return
    match = re.match(r"(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\.([a-z0-9]+)\.mono$", template_version)
    if not match:
        die(f"unexpected Godot version {template_version}")
    tag = f"{match[1]}-{match[2]}"
    url = f"https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/{tag}/Godot_v{tag}_mono_export_templates.tpz"
    say(f"Export templates {template_version}: fetching {', '.join(missing)} into {folder}")
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    whole = None
    try:
        source = io.BufferedReader(RangeReader(url), buffer_size=8 << 20)
    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:
        print(f"    no range requests ({error}): downloading the whole archive", flush=True)
        fd, whole = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".tpz")
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as f, urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as response:
            shutil.copyfileobj(response, f, 1 << 20)
        source = open(whole, "rb")
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(source) as archive:
            for name in missing:  # version.txt last: Godot takes the folder for complete once it is there
                info = archive.getinfo(f"templates/{name}")
                print(f"    {name} ({info.file_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)", flush=True)
                partial = folder / f"{name}.part"
                with archive.open(info) as src, open(partial, "wb") as dst:  # zipfile checks the CRC
                    shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst, 1 << 20)
                os.replace(partial, folder / name)
    finally:
        source.close()
        if whole:
            os.unlink(whole)

    """A remote file read with HTTP range requests, so that zipfile downloads only the members it extracts."""

    def __init__(self, url):
        self.url, self.pos = url, 0
        with self._get(0, 0) as response:
            if response.status != 206:
                raise OSError(f"HTTP {response.status} to a range request")
            self.size = int(response.headers["Content-Range"].rsplit("/", 1)[1])

    def _get(self, first, last):
        request = urllib.request.Request(self.url, headers={"Range": f"bytes={first}-{last}",
                                                            "User-Agent": "marvin-simulator-godot"})
        return urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60)

    def readable(self):
        return True

    def seekable(self):
        return True

    def tell(self):
        return self.pos

    def seek(self, offset, whence=io.SEEK_SET):
        self.pos = {io.SEEK_SET: 0, io.SEEK_CUR: self.pos, io.SEEK_END: self.size}[whence] + offset
        return self.pos

    def readinto(self, buffer):
        end = min(self.pos + len(buffer), self.size)
        if end <= self.pos:
            return 0
        for attempt in range(5):
            try:
                with self._get(self.pos, end - 1) as response:
                    if response.status != 206:
                        raise OSError(f"HTTP {response.status} to a range request")
                    data = response.read()
                break
            except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException):
                if attempt == 4:
                    raise
                time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
        buffer[:len(data)] = data
        self.pos += len(data)
        return len(data)


def templates_folder(template_version):
    if MACOS:
        base = Path.home() / "Library" / "Application Support" / "Godot"
    elif WINDOWS:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("APPDATA") or Path.home() / "AppData" / "Roaming") / "Godot"
    else:
        base = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME") or Path.home() / ".local" / "share") / "godot"
    return base / "export_templates" / template_version


def ensure_templates(folder, template_version, needed):
    """Fetches the export template files the presets need from Godot's release archive (1.2 GB for every platform;
    only the needed members, about 200 MB for both presets, are downloaded)."""
    missing = [name for name in ["icudt_godot.dat", *needed, "version.txt"] if not (folder / name).is_file()]
    if not missing:
        return
    match = re.match(r"(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\.([a-z0-9]+)\.mono$", template_version)
    if not match:
        die(f"unexpected Godot version {template_version}")
    tag = f"{match[1]}-{match[2]}"
    url = f"https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/{tag}/Godot_v{tag}_mono_export_templates.tpz"
    say(f"Export templates {template_version}: fetching {', '.join(missing)} into {folder}")
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    whole = None
    try:
        source = io.BufferedReader(RangeReader(url), buffer_size=8 << 20)
    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as error:
        print(f"    no range requests ({error}): downloading the whole archive", flush=True)
        fd, whole = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".tpz")
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as f, urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as response:
            shutil.copyfileobj(response, f, 1 << 20)
        source = open(whole, "rb")
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(source) as archive:
            for name in missing:  # version.txt last: Godot takes the folder for complete once it is there
                info = archive.getinfo(f"templates/{name}")
                print(f"    {name} ({info.file_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)", flush=True)
                partial = folder / f"{name}.part"
                with archive.open(info) as src, open(partial, "wb") as dst:  # zipfile checks the CRC
                    shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst, 1 << 20)
                os.replace(partial, folder / name)
    finally:
        source.close()
        if whole:
            os.unlink(whole)

def cmd_export(args):
    platforms, mode, pack = [], "release", False
    for arg in args:
        if arg in PRESETS:
            platforms.append(arg)
        elif arg == "--debug":
            mode = "debug"
        elif arg == "--zip":

            die(f"export: unknown argument {arg}\n{EXPORT_HELP}")
    platforms = platforms or (["macos", "windows"] if MACOS else ["windows"])

    version = godot_version(godot)

            print(tail(log), file=sys.stderr)

            status = 1
            continue
        errors = [line for line in log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
                  if re.search(r"(^|m)(ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR):", line)]
        if errors:
            print("\n".join(errors), file=sys.stderr)

    return status

"""Copy the macOS simulator's runtime assets into assets/ (gitignored).

The macOS game is the reference and is never modified. Generated assets
(Marvin geometry.bin, BB8/WallE Generated/) are gitignored there, so by default
they are read from the main checkout; override with MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES.
Run apps/simulator-macos/build-app.sh first if they are missing.
"""
import os, shutil, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
def main_checkout():
    common = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir"],
                            cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    return Path(common).parent if common else root.parent.parent
src = Path(os.environ.get("MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES", main_checkout() / "apps/simulator-macos/Resources"))
dst = root / "assets"
SKIP_SUFFIX = {".zip", ".glb", ".hdr", ".rtf", ".icns"}
FOLDERS = ["Marvin", "R2D2", "BB8", "WallE", "City", "Dirt", "Audio", "Icons"]
TEXTURE_IMPORT = """[remap]

importer="texture"
type="CompressedTexture2D"

[params]

compress/mode=0
mipmaps/generate=true
"""
# Audio is read as raw .wav bytes by the AVAudioFile facade (FileAccess), in the editor and in exports alike: keep the
# files as they are instead of importing them as AudioStreamWAV (Godot's default import compresses them with QOA, which
# an export would then ship instead of the .wav, and the facade cannot decode).
KEEP_IMPORT = """[remap]

importer="keep"
"""

if not (src / "Marvin/geometry.bin").exists():
    sys.exit(f"missing {src}/Marvin/geometry.bin - run apps/simulator-macos/build-app.sh in the main checkout")
copied = 0
for folder in FOLDERS:
    for path in (src / folder).rglob("*"):
        if path.is_dir() or path.suffix.lower() in SKIP_SUFFIX:
            continue
        target = dst / path.relative_to(src)
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if not target.exists() or target.stat().st_mtime < path.stat().st_mtime or target.stat().st_size != path.stat().st_size:
            shutil.copy2(path, target)
            copied += 1
        if path.suffix.lower() in {".jpg", ".png"}:
            imp = target.with_name(target.name + ".import")
            if not imp.exists():
                imp.write_text(TEXTURE_IMPORT)
        if path.suffix.lower() == ".wav":
            imp = target.with_name(target.name + ".import")
            if not imp.exists() or 'importer="keep"' not in imp.read_text():
                imp.write_text(KEEP_IMPORT)
print(f"assets: {copied} files updated from {src}")

output.text:
Script completed
Wall time 0.3 seconds
Output:

{"chunk_id":"23c484","wall_time_seconds":0.000007792,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":3771,"output":"    game's name and icon (macOS takes them from the app's Info.plist, which Godot cannot change at run time; exports
    have their own). The copy is an APFS clone (no extra disk space) with a new Info.plist and icon, signed ad hoc.
    Remade when Godot or the icon changes; on any failure, play runs Godot's own app."""
    source = godot.parent.parent.parent
    if source.suffix != ".app" or source == DEV_APP:
        return godot
    icon = ROOT / "assets" / "Icons" / "AppIconLight.png"
    stamp_file = DEV_APP.parent / "dev-app.stamp"  # outside the signed bundle
    stamp = "\n".join([DEV_APP_VERSION, str(source), str((source / "Contents" / "Info.plist").stat().st_mtime_ns),
                       str(icon.stat().st_mtime_ns) if icon.is_file() else "-"])
    binary = DEV_APP / "Contents" / "MacOS" / godot.name
    if binary.is_file() and stamp_file.is_file() and stamp_file.read_text() == stamp:
        return binary
    say(f"Making {DEV_APP.relative_to(ROOT)} (Godot's app with the game's name and icon)")
    try:
        shutil.rmtree(DEV_APP, ignore_errors=True)
        DEV_APP.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        quiet = {"stdout": subprocess.DEVNULL, "stderr": subprocess.PIPE, "text": True}
        if subprocess.run(["cp", "-cR", source, DEV_APP], **quiet).returncode:  # clone; a copy off APFS
            shutil.copytree(source, DEV_APP, symlinks=True)
        plist = DEV_APP / "Contents" / "Info.plist"
        steps = [["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleName", "-string", "Marvin Simulator", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleDisplayName", "-string", "Marvin Simulator", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleIdentifier", "-string", "io.entire.marvin.simulator.godot.dev", plist],
                 ["plutil", "-remove", "CFBundleDocumentTypes", plist]]
        if icon.is_file():
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
                iconset = Path(tmp) / "Marvin.iconset"
                iconset.mkdir()
                for size in (16, 32, 128, 256, 512):
                    for scale in (1, 2):
                        name = f"icon_{size}x{size}{'@2x' if scale == 2 else ''}.png"
                        run(["sips", "-z", size * scale, size * scale, icon, "--out", iconset / name], **quiet)
                run(["iconutil", "-c", "icns", iconset, "-o", DEV_APP / "Contents" / "Resources" / "Marvin.icns"],
                    **quiet)
            # The asset catalog's icon (CFBundleIconName) takes precedence over CFBundleIconFile.
            steps += [["plutil", "-remove", "CFBundleIconName", plist],
                      ["plutil", "-replace", "CFBundleIconFile", "-string", "Marvin.icns", plist]]
        for step in steps:
            subprocess.run(step, **quiet)  # -remove of a missing key fails harmlessly
        subprocess.run(["xattr", "-dr", "com.apple.quarantine", DEV_APP], **quiet)
        # Only the outer bundle changed: re-sign it ad hoc, keeping Godot's entitlements and hardened runtime.
        signed = subprocess.run(["codesign", "--force", "--sign", "-", "--preserve-metadata=entitlements,flags",
                                 DEV_APP], **quiet)
        if signed.returncode:
            raise OSError(signed.stderr.strip())
        stamp_file.write_text(stamp)
        return binary
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError, SystemExit) as error:
        print(f"    warning: {error or 'failed'}; playing in Godot's own app", flush=True)
        shutil.rmtree(DEV_APP, ignore_errors=True)
        return godot

        if not target.exists() or target.stat().st_mtime < path.stat().st_mtime or target.stat().st_size != path.stat().st_size:
            shutil.copy2(path, target)
            copied += 1
        if path.suffix.lower() in {".jpg", ".png"}:
            imp = target.with_name(target.name + ".import")
            if not imp.exists():
                imp.write_text(TEXTURE_IMPORT)
        if path.suffix.lower() == ".wav":
            imp = target.with_name(target.name + ".import")
            if not imp.exists() or 'importer="keep"' not in imp.read_text():
                imp.write_text(KEEP_IMPORT)
print(f"assets: {copied} files updated from {src}")
"}

PORTING.md:60:**Mirror the Swift code.** Port file by file and keep every type, member and function name **verbatim**, including Swift's camelCase member names. Do not restructure, "improve" or simplify behaviour. If something cannot be mirrored, note the deviation in a `// PORT:` comment.
PORTING.md:215:- **Shadows**: forward shadows remove `shadowColor.alpha` of that light. Deferred shadows leave the light itself unshadowed and multiply the **final** colour (all lights, ambient, sky light, emission) by `1 - alpha x shadow`; faces turned away from the light count as shadowed (thin double-sided planes seen from behind darken too), and a large `shadowRadius` self-shadows lit curved/sloped surfaces as a function of the angle to the light only (measured on spheres of 0.15 m and 1 m, map 2048/4096, orthographicScale 2/10: identical): radius 3 none; 8: plateau 0.28 from 37 deg; 16-32: 0.44 from 27 deg. `shadowBias` has no measurable effect (0.001, 1 and 10 identical, forward and deferred). Shadow maps hold the faces turned towards the light (a single-sided plane shadows what lies under it only when it faces the light). Casters are pushed away from the light by a slope-scaled bias (measured with fixed boxes, `GroundBiasProbe`): a casting ground leaves the sunlit walls standing on it lit down to 2 mm at elevations 5-35 degrees, and a 1 cm plate's shadow on the ground is half there once its gap is about 1.3 cm + 2.2 shadow texels (2.4 / 4.8 / 7.5 / 15 cm for texels of 0.49 / 1.42 / 2.83 / 5.66 cm); lit walls do not self-shadow below 75 degrees to the light. Penumbra (10-90%) of a fixed shadow box is about 1.2 x `shadowRadius` texels of the light's own map in light space (map 4096 over 116 m, radius 3: 11.5 cm on a floor lit at 60 deg). Transparent geometry casts opaque shadows. In the sandbox's deferred setup SceneKit also darkens lit surfaces by 4-6% at grazing view angles (none from above); not reproduced. Measured (`CAL_EXP=deferredview`, Swift twin `sb.swift`/`sbmap.swift`): it depends on the antialiasing mode, as if the deferred pass rebuilt the position from the depth of MSAA sample 0 (4x: 0.375 px up from the pixel centre, which puts it below a floor receding upwards) along the ray through the pixel centre: with shadow alpha 1 the far floor is 70% shadowed with 4x MSAA, 7% without antialiasing and none with 2x (sample 0 below the centre); the shadowed share grows with that point's drop below the surface (0.2-0.3 at under 1 mm, 0.4-0.8 at 3-5 mm) but differs between views at equal drops, and without antialiasing it is still 2-13%. Moving Godot's shadow lookup to the same point (`LIGHT_VERTEX`) changes nothing: Godot's shadow biases absorb millimetre offsets.
PORTING.md:257:**Graphics-detail variants** (Godot-only, look changes, never at Graphics detail Max; `SceneKitRuntime.DetailVariant`, "Known deviations"). `SceneKitCalibration.SimpleSkyReflection` adds `VariantFlags.SimpleSky` to every scene's variant: physically based materials whose roughness no shader modifier changes (everything but the robots, whose `DirtCoating` modifier writes `ROUGHNESS`, so their chrome keeps the sharp horizon of the radiance bands) take their sky reflection from the sky light's spherical harmonics at the reflection direction (`scn_irradiance(scn_refl)`) instead of `scn_env_radiance` (the equirect mapping and two texture fetches). `SimpleGroundLighting` adds `VariantFlags.SimpleGround`: blended physically based materials that write no depth (the town's ground overlays: trampled sand, streets, doorway patches, aprons) get no direct specular term in `light()` and the same spherical-harmonics sky reflection. A change at run time bumps `SceneKitRuntime.DetailEpoch`; each scene rebuilds its nodes with the new variants before a view draws it next (`ObserveShading`) or when it is prepared (`PrepareAsync`: a race world cached from an earlier race rebuilds behind the loading screen).
PORTING.md:354:- `SCNLight`: directional/omni/spot -> `Light3D` child of the node (energy = intensity/1000, colour linearised then re-encoded, `temperature` tint). Ambient lights feed `scn_ambient`. Shadows: `ShadowOpacity` = shadow alpha (forward) or 1 (deferred, see the composer's `light()`); single orthogonal split for one cascade; `DirectionalShadowMaxDistance` = `min(maximumShadowDistance, max(4 x orthographicScale, 10))` when SceneKit adjusts the projection. A fixed box (up to two lights) is reproduced per camera: the composer's `light()` treats receivers outside the box as unshadowed, and `FitShadows` keeps the calibrated single split up to `min(maximumShadowDistance, orthographicScale)` from the camera; when the box reaches further into the view (the farthest view depth of box ∩ frustum, `SCNLight.ShadowBoxFarDepth`), it switches to two splits (`Parallel2Splits`, no blending) with the calibrated fit as the first split and the second out to that depth. Godot halves the light's atlas region for splits (its normal-bias texel doubles, so the normal bias is halved: `SplitNormalBiasExponent`) and scales the second split's PCF kernel by split1/split2, which keeps its world size within about 10%. The directional shadow atlas is 8192 (two 4096-class suns), hard filter (SoftHigh in the exact configuration: Shadow quality Exact on the Settings screen, or `MARVIN_SCN_CAL=Exact`; see "Known deviations"). Under the hard filter the fixed boxes get four splits instead (`SceneKitRuntime.NearSplitDistances`, `SceneKitCalibration.HardShadowSplit1`/`HardShadowSplit2`): ending 12 and 30 m from the camera, at `orthographicScale` and at the box's farthest view depth rounded up to steps of 25 % (`HardShadowFarStep`), each a quarter of the light's atlas region (2048 x 4096). The distances are fixed in metres, so Godot's texel snapping (each split's square light-space extent comes from the bounding sphere of its frustum slice) keeps the first three splits still while the camera moves; the last one changes only at a step. With the race camera at 1080p the texels are 1.2 / 2.8 / 5.3 / 14 cm across the light and half that along its y axis, instead of 2.9 cm to 58 m and 7 cm beyond. The race world's flat base terrain does not cast under the hard filter (`SceneKitCalibration.BaseTerrainCastsShadow`): it shadows nothing visible but filled every split, and leaving it out pays for the extra splits (`docs/performance.md`, "Near shadow splits").

PORTING.md:483:Measured on macOS 27 with offline AVAudioEngine renders and reproduced (`tools/godot -- --audio-facade-test DIR` checks 66 values against the macOS numbers): source volume/pan apply at the downstream mixer input even through effects; pan is a balance law; mixer gains slew per channel at 1/1200 per frame (first render snaps, a stopped direct player freezes its ramp); `outputVolume` ramps over one render; varispeed rate applies per render with a 48-frame input delay; `.lowPass` is a bilinear Butterworth whose frequency glides log-linearly over 1440 frames; AUPeakLimiter (lookahead 96 frames, ramp slope `(-peak dB - gain dB)/86` per frame, ramps restarted by louder peaks, hold while a peak is in the window, release half-life 5 ms) matches Apple's output within 1e-5 on tones, spikes and noise; `play()` starts at the engine's sample time on the player's own render timeline, so offline a restarted loop behind a slowed varispeed stays silent until it catches up (as in the macOS evidence WAVs), while a real-time engine restarts its timeline. A running real-time engine renders on its own thread into a 48 kHz `AudioStreamGenerator` (`AVAudioEngineOutput` under the root, about 32 ms queued; 100 ms on the headless Dummy driver). `--audio-smoke-test` renders the same evidence WAVs and `audio.json` as macOS: per-stage levels match within 0.2 dB (Marvin, city and storm within 0.04 dB), whole-file levels within 0.06 dB. Deviations: the resampler is a 24-tap windowed sinc rather than Apple's converter (residual interpolation differences, about 0.1 dB per second of motor sound); the residual burst after an offline restart is about 1 dB weaker; raw `.wav` files are read from `res://assets/Audio` (exports fall back to Godot's imported 16-bit PCM).

Deferred shadows leave the light itself unshadowed and multiply the **final** colour (all lights, ambient, sky light, emission) by `1 - alpha x shadow`; faces turned away from the light count as shadowed (thin double-sided planes seen from behind darken too), and a large `shadowRadius` self-shadows lit curved/sloped surfaces as a function of the angle to the light only (measured on spheres of 0.15 m and 1 m, map 2048/4096, orthographicScale 2/10: identical): radius 3 none; 8: plateau 0.28 from 37 deg; 16-32: 0.44 from 27 deg. `shadowBias` has no measurable effect (0.001, 1 and 10 identical, forward and deferred). Shadow maps hold the faces turned towards the light (a single-sided plane shadows what lies under it only when it faces the light). Casters are pushed away from the light by a slope-scaled bias (measured with fixed boxes, `GroundBiasProbe`): a casting ground leaves the sunlit walls standing on it lit down to 2 mm at elevations 5-35 degrees, and a 1 cm plate's shadow on the ground is half there once its gap is about 1.3 cm + 2.2 shadow texels (2.4 / 4.8 / 7.5 / 15 cm for texels of 0.49 / 1.42 / 2.83 / 5.66 cm); lit walls do not self-shadow below 75 degrees to the light. Penumbra (10-90%) of a fixed shadow box is about 1.2 x `shadowRadius` texels of the light's own map in light space (map 4096 over 116 m, radius 3: 11.5 cm on a floor lit at 60 deg). Transparent geometry casts opaque shadows. In the sandbox's deferred setup SceneKit also darkens lit surfaces by 4-6% at grazing view angles (none from above); not reproduced. Measured (`CAL_EXP=deferredview`, Swift twin `sb.swift`/`sbmap.swift`): it depends on the antialiasing mode, as if the deferred pass rebuilt the position from the depth of MSAA sample 0 (4x: 0.375 px up from the pixel centre, which puts it below a floor receding upwards) along the ray through the pixel centre: with shadow alpha 1 the far floor is 70% shadowed with 4x MSAA, 7% without antialiasing and none with 2x (sample 0 below the centre); the shadowed share grows with that point's drop below the surface (0.2-0.3 at under 1 mm, 0.4-0.8 at 3-5 mm) but differs between views at equal drops, and without antialiasing it is still 2-13%. PORTING.md:215:- **Shadows**: forward shadows remove `shadowColor.alpha` of that light. Deferred shadows leave the light itself unshadowed and multiply the **final** colour (all lights, ambient, sky light, emission) by `1 - alpha x shadow`; faces turned away from the light count as shadowed (thin double-sided planes seen from behind darken too), and a large `shadowRadius` self-shadows lit curved/sloped surfaces as a function of the angle to the light only (measured on spheres of 0.15 m and 1 m, map 2048/4096, orthographicScale 2/10: identical): radius 3 none; 8: plateau 0.28 from 37 deg; 16-32: 0.44 from 27 deg. `shadowBias` has no measurable effect (0.001, 1 and 10 identical, forward and deferred). Shadow maps hold the faces turned towards the light (a single-sided plane shadows what lies under it only when it faces the light). Casters are pushed away from the light by a slope-scaled bias (measured with fixed boxes, `GroundBiasProbe`): a casting ground leaves the sunlit walls standing on it lit down to 2 mm at elevations 5-35 degrees, and a 1 cm plate's shadow on the ground is half there once its gap is about 1.3 cm + 2.2 shadow texels (2.4 / 4.8 / 7.5 / 15 cm for texels of 0.49 / 1.42 / 2.83 / 5.66 cm); lit walls do not self-shadow below 75 degrees to the light. Penumbra (10-90%) of a fixed shadow box is about 1.2 x `shadowRadius` texels of the light's own map in light space (map 4096 over 116 m, radius 3: 11.5 cm on a floor lit at 60 deg). Transparent geometry casts opaque shadows. In the sandbox's deferred setup SceneKit also darkens lit surfaces by 4-6% at grazing view angles (none from above); not reproduced. Measured (`CAL_EXP=deferredview`, Swift twin `sb.swift`/`sbmap.swift`): it depends on the antialiasing mode, as if the deferred pass rebuilt the position from the depth of MSAA sample 0 (4x: 0.375 px up from the pixel centre, which puts it below a floor receding upwards) along the ray through the pixel centre: with shadow alpha 1 the far floor is 70% shadowed with 4x MSAA, 7% without antialiasing and none with 2x (sample 0 below the centre); the shadowed share grows with that point's drop below the surface (0.2-0.3 at under 1 mm, 0.4-0.8 at 3-5 mm) but differs between views at equal drops, and without antialiasing it is still 2-13%. Moving Godot's shadow lookup to the same point (`LIGHT_VERTEX`) changes nothing: Godot's shadow biases absorb millimetre offsets.
PORTING.md:257:**Graphics-detail variants** (Godot-only, look changes, never at Graphics detail Max; `SceneKitRuntime.DetailVariant`, "Known deviations"). `SceneKitCalibration.SimpleSkyReflection` adds `VariantFlags.SimpleSky` to every scene's variant: physically based materials whose roughness no shader modifier changes (everything but the robots, whose `DirtCoating` modifier writes `ROUGHNESS`, so their chrome keeps the sharp horizon of the radiance bands) take their sky reflection from the sky light's spherical harmonics at the reflection direction (`scn_irradiance(scn_refl)`) instead of `scn_env_radiance` (the equirect mapping and two texture fetches). `SimpleGroundLighting` adds `VariantFlags.SimpleGround`: blended physically based materials that write no depth (the town's ground overlays: trampled sand, streets, doorway patches, aprons) get no direct specular term in `light()` and the same spherical-harmonics sky reflection. A change at run time bumps `SceneKitRuntime.DetailEpoch`; each scene rebuilds its nodes with the new variants before a view draws it next (`ObserveShading`) or when it is prepared (`PrepareAsync`: a race world cached from an earlier race rebuilds behind the loading screen).
PORTING.md:354:- `SCNLight`: directional/omni/spot -> `Light3D` child of the node (energy = intensity/1000, colour linearised then re-encoded, `temperature` tint). Ambient lights feed `scn_ambient`. Shadows: `ShadowOpacity` = shadow alpha (forward) or 1 (deferred, see the composer's `light()`); single orthogonal split for one cascade; `DirectionalShadowMaxDistance` = `min(maximumShadowDistance, max(4 x orthographicScale, 10))` when SceneKit adjusts the projection. A fixed box (up to two lights) is reproduced per camera: the composer's `light()` treats receivers outside the box as unshadowed, and `FitShadows` keeps the calibrated single split up to `min(maximumShadowDistance, orthographicScale)` from the camera; when the box reaches further into the view (the farthest view depth of box ∩ frustum, `SCNLight.ShadowBoxFarDepth`), it switches to two splits (`Parallel2Splits`, no blending) with the calibrated fit as the first split and the second out to that depth. Godot halves the light's atlas region for splits (its normal-bias texel doubles, so the normal bias is halved: `SplitNormalBiasExponent`) and scales the second split's PCF kernel by split1/split2, which keeps its world size within about 10%. The directional shadow atlas is 8192 (two 4096-class suns), hard filter (SoftHigh in the exact configuration: Shadow quality Exact on the Settings screen, or `MARVIN_SCN_CAL=Exact`; see "Known deviations"). Under the hard filter the fixed boxes get four splits instead (`SceneKitRuntime.NearSplitDistances`, `SceneKitCalibration.HardShadowSplit1`/`HardShadowSplit2`): ending 12 and 30 m from the camera, at `orthographicScale` and at the box's farthest view depth rounded up to steps of 25 % (`HardShadowFarStep`), each a quarter of the light's atlas region (2048 x 4096). The distances are fixed in metres, so Godot's texel snapping (each split's square light-space extent comes from the bounding sphere of its frustum slice) keeps the first three splits still while the camera moves; the last one changes only at a step. With the race camera at 1080p the texels are 1.2 / 2.8 / 5.3 / 14 cm across the light and half that along its y axis, instead of 2.9 cm to 58 m and 7 cm beyond. The race world's flat base terrain does not cast under the hard filter (`SceneKitCalibration.BaseTerrainCastsShadow`): it shadows nothing visible but filled every split, and leaving it out pays for the extra splits (`docs/performance.md`, "Near shadow splits").

## Memory

You have access to a memory folder with guidance from prior runs. It can save
time and help you stay consistent. Use it whenever it is likely to help.

Decision boundary: should you use memory for a new user query?

- Skip memory ONLY when the request is clearly self-contained and does not need
  workspace history, conventions, or prior decisions.
- Hard skip examples: current time/date, simple translation, simple sentence
  rewrite, one-line shell command, trivial formatting.
- Use memory by default when ANY of these are true:
  - the query mentions workspace/repo/module/path/files in MEMORY_SUMMARY below,
  - the user asks for prior context / consistency / previous decisions,
  - the task is ambiguous and could depend on earlier project choices,
  - the ask is a non-trivial and related to MEMORY_SUMMARY below.
- If unsure, do a quick memory pass.

Memory layout (general -> specific):

- /Users/thomi/.codex/memories/memory_summary.md (already provided below; do NOT open again)
- /Users/thomi/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md (searchable registry; primary file to query)
- /Users/thomi/.codex/memories/skills/<skill-name>/ (skill folder)
  - SKILL.md (entrypoint instructions)
  - scripts/ (optional helper scripts)
  - examples/ (optional example outputs)
  - templates/ (optional templates)
- /Users/thomi/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ (per-rollout recaps + evidence snippets)
  - The paths of these entries can be found in /Users/thomi/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md or /Users/thomi/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ as `rollout_path`
  - These files are append-only `jsonl`: `session_meta.payload.id` identifies the session, `turn_context` marks turn boundaries, `event_msg` is the lightweight status stream, and `response_item` contains actual messages, tool calls, and tool outputs.
  - For efficient lookup, prefer matching the filename suffix or `session_meta.payload.id`; avoid broad full-content scans unless needed.

Quick memory pass (when applicable):

1. Skim the MEMORY_SUMMARY below and extract task-relevant keywords.
2. Search /Users/thomi/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md using those keywords.
3. Only if MEMORY.md directly points to rollout summaries/skills, open the 1-2
   most relevant files under /Users/thomi/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ or
   /Users/thomi/.codex/memories/skills/.
4. If above are not clear and you need exact commands, error text, or precise evidence, search over `rollout_path` for more evidence.
5. If there are no relevant hits, stop memory lookup and continue normally.

Quick-pass budget:

- Keep memory lookup lightweight: ideally <= 4-6 search steps before main work.
- Avoid broad scans of all rollout summaries.

During execution: if you hit repeated errors, confusing behavior, or suspect
relevant prior context, redo the quick memory pass.

How to decide whether to verify memory:

- Consider both risk of drift and verification effort.
- If a fact is likely to drift and is cheap to verify, verify it before
  answering.
- If a fact is likely to drift but verification is expensive, slow, or
  disruptive, it is acceptable to answer from memory in an interactive turn,
  but you should say that it is memory-derived, note that it may be stale, and
  consider offering to refresh it live.
- If a fact is lower-drift and expensive to verify, it is usually fine to
  answer from memory directly.

When answering from memory without current verification:

- If you rely on memory for a fact that you did not verify in the current turn,
  say so briefly in the final answer.
- If that fact is plausibly drift-prone or comes from an older note, older
  snapshot, or prior run summary, say that it may be stale or outdated.
- If live verification was skipped and a refresh would be useful in the
  interactive context, consider offering to verify or refresh it live.
- Do not present unverified memory-derived facts as confirmed-current.
- Prefer a short refresh offer for interactive questions, especially about prior
  results, commands, timing, or older snapshots.

Memory citation requirements:

- If ANY relevant memory files were used: append exactly one
`<oai-mem-citation>` block as the VERY LAST content of the final reply.
  Normal responses should include the answer first, then append the
`<oai-mem-citation>` block at the end.
- Use this exact structure for programmatic parsing:
```
<oai-mem-citation>
<citation_entries>
MEMORY.md:234-236|note=[responsesapi citation extraction code pointer]
rollout_summaries/2026-02-17T21-23-02-LN3m-example.md:10-12|note=[weekly report format]
</citation_entries>
<rollout_ids>
019c6e27-e55b-73d1-87d8-4e01f1f75043
019c7714-3b77-74d1-9866-e1f484aae2ab
</rollout_ids>
</oai-mem-citation>
```
- `citation_entries` is for rendering:
  - one citation entry per line
  - format: `<file>:<line_start>-<line_end>|note=[<how memory was used>]`
  - use file paths relative to the memory base path (for example, `MEMORY.md`,
    `rollout_summaries/...`, `skills/...`)
  - only cite files actually used under the memory base path (do not cite
    workspace files as memory citations)
  - if you used `MEMORY.md` and then a rollout summary/skill file, cite both
  - list entries in order of importance (most important first)
  - `note` should be short, single-line, and use simple characters only (avoid
    unusual symbols, no newlines)
- `rollout_ids` is for us to track what previous rollouts you find useful:
  - include one rollout id per line
  - rollout ids should look like UUIDs (for example,

  - do not include file paths or notes in this section
  - For every `citation_entries`, try to find and cite the corresponding rollout id if possible
- Never include memory citations inside pull-request messages.
- Never cite blank lines; double-check ranges.

Updating memories:

You can update the memories **only** when explicitly asked by the user. This must always come from a direct request from the user.
- Write your update in /Users/thomi/.codex/memories/extensions/ad_hoc/notes/
- Each update must be one small file containing what you want to add/delete/update from the memories.
