#!/bin/sh
set -eu
root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
status() {
  if [ "${MARVIN_PROGRESS:-}" = 1 ]; then
    printf '\036%s\n' "$1"
  else
    printf '\n%s\n' "$1"
  fi
}
status 'Preparing Swift tools'
# Use the installed standalone CLT if Xcode is selected but unavailable (for
# example, awaiting a license agreement). Do not change the global selection.
if ! /usr/bin/xcrun --find swift >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -x /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/swift ]; then
  export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools
fi
# Swift Build's Xcode-oriented backend adds framework/library search paths
# absent from standalone CLT and requests the legacy arclite support library.
# Use SwiftPM's native backend for CLT; retain the default with full Xcode.
# Keep this selection identical for the build and its output-path lookup.
set --
case "${DEVELOPER_DIR:-$(/usr/bin/xcode-select -p)}" in
  */CommandLineTools|*/CommandLineTools/)
    set -- --build-system native
    ;;
esac
configuration=${CONFIGURATION:-release}
status 'Checking model assets'
python3 "$root/scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py"
python3 "$root/scripts/city/check-assets.py"
status "Building Marvin Simulator ($configuration)"
swift build "$@" --package-path "$root/apps/simulator-macos" -c "$configuration" --product MarvinSimulator
bin=$(swift build "$@" --package-path "$root/apps/simulator-macos" -c "$configuration" --show-bin-path)
app="$root/apps/simulator-macos/.build/Marvin Simulator.app"
status 'Packaging Marvin Simulator'
mkdir -p "$app/Contents/MacOS" "$app/Contents/Resources"
cp "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Info.plist" "$app/Contents/Info.plist"
cp "$bin/MarvinSimulator" "$app/Contents/MacOS/MarvinSimulator.new"
mv -f "$app/Contents/MacOS/MarvinSimulator.new" "$app/Contents/MacOS/MarvinSimulator"
# Replace this generated bundle directory so retired model files cannot linger.
rm -rf "$app/Contents/Resources/R2D2" "$app/Contents/Resources/BB8" "$app/Contents/Resources/WallE"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/R2D2" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/BB8" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/WallE" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
rm -rf "$app/Contents/Resources/City"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/City" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/Dirt" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/Marvin" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/Icons/"*.icns "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp "$root/LICENSE-hardware" "$app/Contents/Resources/LICENSE-hardware"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/Audio" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/Audio/Credits.rtf" "$app/Contents/Resources/Credits.rtf"
status 'Signing Marvin Simulator'
codesign --force --sign - "$app"
printf '\nBuilt: %s\n' "$app"

#!/bin/sh
set -eu
root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
status() {
  if [ "${MARVIN_PROGRESS:-}" = 1 ]; then
    printf '\036%s\n' "$1"
  else
    printf '\n%s\n' "$1"
  fi
}
status 'Preparing Swift tools'
# Use the installed standalone CLT if Xcode is selected but unavailable (for
# example, awaiting a license agreement). Do not change the global selection.
if ! /usr/bin/xcrun --find swift >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -x /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/swift ]; then
  export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools
fi
# Swift Build's Xcode-oriented backend adds framework/library search paths
# absent from standalone CLT and requests the legacy arclite support library.
# Use SwiftPM's native backend for CLT; retain the default with full Xcode.
# Keep this selection identical for the build and its output-path lookup.
set --
case "${DEVELOPER_DIR:-$(/usr/bin/xcode-select -p)}" in
  */CommandLineTools|*/CommandLineTools/)
    set -- --build-system native
    ;;
esac
configuration=${CONFIGURATION:-release}
status 'Checking model assets'
python3 "$root/scripts/prepare-simulator-assets.py"
python3 "$root/scripts/city/check-assets.py"
status "Building Marvin Simulator ($configuration)"
swift build "$@" --package-path "$root/apps/simulator-macos" -c "$configuration" --product MarvinSimulator
bin=$(swift build "$@" --package-path "$root/apps/simulator-macos" -c "$configuration" --show-bin-path)
app="$root/apps/simulator-macos/.build/Marvin Simulator.app"
status 'Packaging Marvin Simulator'
mkdir -p "$app/Contents/MacOS" "$app/Contents/Resources"
cp "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Info.plist" "$app/Contents/Info.plist"
cp "$bin/MarvinSimulator" "$app/Contents/MacOS/MarvinSimulator.new"
mv -f "$app/Contents/MacOS/MarvinSimulator.new" "$app/Contents/MacOS/MarvinSimulator"
# Replace this generated bundle directory so retired model files cannot linger.
rm -rf "$app/Contents/Resources/R2D2" "$app/Contents/Resources/BB8" "$app/Contents/Resources/WallE"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/R2D2" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/BB8" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/WallE" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
rm -rf "$app/Contents/Resources/City"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/City" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/Dirt" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/Marvin" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/Icons/"*.icns "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp "$root/LICENSE-hardware" "$app/Contents/Resources/LICENSE-hardware"
cp -R "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/Audio" "$app/Contents/Resources/"
cp "$root/apps/simulator-macos/Resources/Audio/Credits.rtf" "$app/Contents/Resources/Credits.rtf"
status 'Signing Marvin Simulator'
codesign --force --sign - "$app"
printf '\nBuilt: %s\n' "$app"
"}

apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:42:apps/simulator-godot/tools/godot -- --hud-smoke-test DIR     # HUD/loading/sandbox HUD captures + hud-smoke.json (compare with tools/scenekit-reference/ui-reference/build.sh)
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:257:**Graphics-detail variants** (Godot-only, look changes, never at Graphics detail Max; `SceneKitRuntime.DetailVariant`, "Known deviations"). `SceneKitCalibration.SimpleSkyReflection` adds `VariantFlags.SimpleSky` to every scene's variant: physically based materials whose roughness no shader modifier changes (everything but the robots, whose `DirtCoating` modifier writes `ROUGHNESS`, so their chrome keeps the sharp horizon of the radiance bands) take their sky reflection from the sky light's spherical harmonics at the reflection direction (`scn_irradiance(scn_refl)`) instead of `scn_env_radiance` (the equirect mapping and two texture fetches). `SimpleGroundLighting` adds `VariantFlags.SimpleGround`: blended physically based materials that write no depth (the town's ground overlays: trampled sand, streets, doorway patches, aprons) get no direct specular term in `light()` and the same spherical-harmonics sky reflection. A change at run time bumps `SceneKitRuntime.DetailEpoch`; each scene rebuilds its nodes with the new variants before a view draws it next (`ObserveShading`) or when it is prepared (`PrepareAsync`: a race world cached from an earlier race rebuilds behind the loading screen).
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:360:- **Render scale and upscaling** (Godot-only, the Graphics detail setting; `SCNView.ApplyRenderScaling`). At `SceneKitCalibration.RenderScale` 1 (Graphics detail Max) an `SCNView`'s viewport renders at the drawable's size with `Msaa3D` from `antialiasingMode`, as before. Below 1 the 3D scene is drawn at that fraction of the drawable's width and height and upscaled to it by Godot (`Viewport.Scaling3DMode`/`Scaling3DScale`): by default with a temporal upscaler, chosen once from what the device offers (`Upscalers`, printed at first use): MetalFX temporal on the Metal driver when the device supports it at that scale (this M2: input scales 0.333-1), else FSR 2.2 (every RenderingDevice driver: Metal, Direct3D 12, Vulkan), else bilinear (no RenderingDevice). Both temporal upscalers accumulate jittered frames (Godot's jitter sequence of 8 / scale^2 phases, its mipmap bias of log2(scale), motion vectors from the depth reprojection plus a motion pass for moved instances) and replace 3D MSAA, which the facade turns off for them (Godot turns it off under MetalFX temporal itself, with a warning). `RenderUpscaler` 1-4 selects bilinear, FSR 1, MetalFX spatial or FSR 2 instead (measurements). Godot upscales after the transparent pass, so glow and tone mapping run at the drawable's size, and the AppKit overlays (HUD, menus, loading screen) are separate controls drawn over the view's texture: they stay at full resolution. `SceneKitCalibration.AnisotropicFiltering` sets the viewports' anisotropy level and `MeshLodThreshold` their mesh LOD threshold. The SSAO port keeps its disk's footprint at the drawable's size (its radius in pixels is scaled by the render scale, so the occlusion keeps its world size), and `SsaoEnabled` false skips it (the effect stops asking Godot for the normal-roughness buffer and clears `scn_ssao` to 1). Under a temporal upscaler `snapshot()` draws the view once per jitter phase (at most 32) so the upscaler's history converges on the still view, as on screen when the camera rests. `SCNRenderer` (offscreen snapshots of the test modes) always renders at full resolution with MSAA.
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:363:- `SCNView`/`SCNRenderer.prepare(_:completionHandler:)` is asynchronous, as in SceneKit (`SceneKitRuntime.PrepareAsync`): the scene's mesh arrays and procedural textures (mipmaps) are computed on worker threads, the main thread hands the nodes whose data is ready to Godot for at most 10 ms per frame, and the handler runs when all of them are flushed; the game keeps the loading screen up meanwhile. `prepare(_:shouldAbortBlock:)`, snapshots and `SCNTransaction.flush()` flush everything at once (`FlushAll`). Material properties whose contents are `res://` image paths start loading the imported texture on Godot's loader threads when the contents are set (`NSImage.Preload`), so a scene built on a background queue finds them loaded.
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:379:**Windows, toolbars and menus** (`NSWindow.cs`, `NSToolbar.cs`, `NSMenu.cs`, `NSLayoutConstraint.cs`). `NSWindow(contentRect:styleMask:backing:defer:)` adopts the Godot window and gives it the content size (in points: on a HiDPI screen the window has `backingScaleFactor` pixels per point through Godot's content scale). With `.fullSizeContentView` the content view fills the client area and the facade draws the title bar over it; on macOS Godot's `extend_to_title` makes the client area the whole window, so the system adds only the traffic lights (moved to the measured centres) and the window has the Mac game's 1280 x 820 frame. The measurements come from `tools/scenekit-reference/WindowChrome.swift`, which builds App.swift's window and toolbar **linked against the macOS 13 SDK like the game** (newer SDKs get AppKit's macOS 26 style: 32/66-point bars, glass buttons): an opaque (236, 235, 234) title bar of 28 points, 52 with the unified toolbar; the title centred (13 pt bold, baseline 18) or at x 92 (15 pt semibold, baseline 30); toolbar items right-aligned, 14 points apart and 15 from the edge, each as wide as its 11-pt label, icon centred at y 21 and label baseline at 46. `tools/godot -- --window-chrome DIR BG.png` renders the same states; against AppKit (inactive window colours, the traffic lights excluded) the bars differ by 0.7 (title bar) and 1.1-1.3/255 (toolbar); title and item positions match within 1 point (AppKit moves Main Menu and Camera 4 points closer once Pause reads Resume). SF Symbols are Apple artwork and are drawn as vector stand-ins (house, video, pause/play, arrow, keyboard). Active-window colours (title 85 % black, icons and labels 60 %) are AppKit's label colours; only the inactive ones could be measured. Clicking a toolbar item calls its action (pressed items darken); the bar drags and zooms the window on macOS. `contentLayoutRect` is the client area below the bar (1280 x 792, or 1280 x 768 with the toolbar), and constraints to `contentLayoutGuide` are re-solved when the toolbar is shown, hidden or replaced and when the window resizes. The game never hides its toolbar: without buttons (main menu, loading, post-race departure) it puts an empty toolbar in the window (`toolbarControlsVisible`), so the bar keeps its 52 points and the title stays on the left; `--window-chrome` also captures that state (window-toolbar-empty.png, the same 1280 x 768 layout as AppKit's). `NSApp.mainMenu` becomes the macOS global menu bar (the first menu's items join the system application menu, which already has Quit); elsewhere the facade draws it in the title bar's left part (Windows has no global menu). Key equivalents are matched in `NSApplicationHost._Input` before the first responder sees the key (AppKit's performKeyEquivalent): Command on macOS, Control elsewhere, where the facade reports Control as `.command` (so `SimulatorView` passes Control-R on instead of driving with R). Application focus, the close request and window focus/minimise reach the `NSApplicationDelegate`/`NSWindowDelegate` methods.
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:386:- **Font smoothing.** CoreText dilates glyphs as a function of the point size, the text colour's luminance and the drawing path (measured over black, grey and white backgrounds, which make no difference): stem gain = min(0.71, size x (0.014 + 0.020 f(L))) px with f(L) = clamp((L - 0.06)/0.94, 0, 1)^0.7, + 0.31 px for control cells (NSTextField, borderless NSButton) drawing over their transparent background (`FontSmoothing`, `SceneKitCalibration.FontSmoothing*`). White text is dilated up to 2.4 times more than black text; the menu's selected button title ("Sandbox", white, cell) was 13 % too light with the old single dilation and the loading screen's light labels 5-13 %. Godot emulates the gain with FreeType emboldening (`NSFont.RenderFont(gain)`, cached per 1/32 px), which widens glyphs to the right, so glyphs are drawn 0.125 x gain further left; `FontDilationRise` (-0.25) lowers the emboldened cap top.
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:389:Calibration: `tools/scenekit-reference/TextCalibration.swift` (CoreText: 28 system/monospaced fonts x 12 cases, glyph positions, 39 string sizes) against `tools/godot -- --text-calibration DIR`, compared by `tools/scenekit-reference/text_calibration.py MAC GODOT [--fit]`: ink within 1.5 % mean (max 5.7 %), vertical ink profiles 3.2 %, glyph positions within 0.2 px. UI references: `tools/scenekit-reference/ui-reference/build.sh DIR` compiles the macOS game's own RaceHUD, RaceNavigationMap, SimulatorView (HUDView) and FrameRateHUD with a copy of SimulationCore and renders the `--hud-smoke-test` states with AppKit; its dirt-hud.png is byte-identical to the game's own smoke capture. Measured (mean |difference| /255, Godot vs AppKit): every HUD state 0.005-0.55 (dirt-hud 0.20, race results 0.24, race start/pause/scores 0.50-0.55, sandbox HUD 0.10, FPS 0.005); vs the game's captures: driving-assist settings 0.18 (0.76 since the Godot-only Shadow quality row, Known deviations), main menu controls 0.23, loading 0.07.
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:453:- **Graphics detail setting** (Godot-only; the macOS Settings screen has no such control: SceneKit draws the full look at 60 FPS on the Mac's GPU). The eighth settings row, "Graphics detail: Max / High / Medium / Low", after Shadow quality (`MainMenuView.graphicsDetail`, `scripts/UI/GraphicsDetailSetting.cs`; activating it cycles Max, High, Medium, Low). **Max**, the default, is the renderer as before the setting: its captures are pixel-identical to the build before and its frame rate the same (the same composed shaders; at 1920 x 1080 the town roam runs at 54.9 FPS in both builds and the race within its run-to-run spread over eight interleaved rounds). using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Reflection;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Godot;

namespace Marvin;

/// Marks a static method `Task Run(string dir, SceneTree tree)` (or `void Run(...)`) as a command-line
/// mode, e.g. [GameMode("--town-smoke-test")]. Main runs it when the flag is passed after "--":
///   tools/godot -- --town-smoke-test captures/town
/// Mirror the macOS flag names and output file names so captures can be compared side by side.
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method, AllowMultiple = true)]
public sealed class GameModeAttribute : Attribute
{
    public string Flag { get; }
    public GameModeAttribute(string flag) { Flag = flag; }
}

public static class GameModes
{
    static Dictionary<string, MethodInfo> modes;

    public static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, MethodInfo> All
    {
        get
        {
            if (modes != null) return modes;
            modes = new Dictionary<string, MethodInfo>();
            foreach (var type in typeof(GameModes).Assembly.GetTypes())
                foreach (var method in type.GetMethods(BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic))
                    foreach (var attribute in method.GetCustomAttributes<GameModeAttribute>())
                    {
                        if (modes.ContainsKey(attribute.Flag)) throw new InvalidOperationException($"duplicate game mode {attribute.Flag}");
                        modes[attribute.Flag] = method;
                    }
            return modes;
        }
    }

    /// Resolves a mode's output directory like the macOS app: relative paths are relative to the working directory.
    public static string OutputDirectory(string arg, string fallback)
    {
        string dir = string.IsNullOrEmpty(arg) || arg.StartsWith("--") ? fallback : arg;
        // The modes write with System.IO, which does not know Godot's user:// (it would create a "user:" folder).
        if (dir.StartsWith("user://")) dir = ProjectSettings.GlobalizePath(dir);
        if (!dir.StartsWith("res://") && !dir.StartsWith("user://") && !System.IO.Path.IsPathRooted(dir))
            dir = System.IO.Path.GetFullPath(dir, System.IO.Directory.GetCurrentDirectory());
        if (!dir.StartsWith("res://") && !dir.StartsWith("user://")) System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(dir);
        return dir;
    }

    /// Runs the first registered mode found in args. Returns false when no mode flag is present.
    public static async Task<bool> TryRun(string[] args, SceneTree tree)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < args.Length; i++)
        {
            if (!All.TryGetValue(args[i], out var method)) continue;
            string dir = OutputDirectory(i + 1 < args.Length ? args[i + 1] : null, "user://" + args[i].TrimStart('-'));
            var result = method.Invoke(null, new object[] { dir, tree });
            if (result is Task task) await task;
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}

apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:257:**Graphics-detail variants** (Godot-only, look changes, never at Graphics detail Max; `SceneKitRuntime.DetailVariant`, "Known deviations"). `SceneKitCalibration.SimpleSkyReflection` adds `VariantFlags.SimpleSky` to every scene's variant: physically based materials whose roughness no shader modifier changes (everything but the robots, whose `DirtCoating` modifier writes `ROUGHNESS`, so their chrome keeps the sharp horizon of the radiance bands) take their sky reflection from the sky light's spherical harmonics at the reflection direction (`scn_irradiance(scn_refl)`) instead of `scn_env_radiance` (the equirect mapping and two texture fetches). `SimpleGroundLighting` adds `VariantFlags.SimpleGround`: blended physically based materials that write no depth (the town's ground overlays: trampled sand, streets, doorway patches, aprons) get no direct specular term in `light()` and the same spherical-harmonics sky reflection. A change at run time bumps `SceneKitRuntime.DetailEpoch`; each scene rebuilds its nodes with the new variants before a view draws it next (`ObserveShading`) or when it is prepared (`PrepareAsync`: a race world cached from an earlier race rebuilds behind the loading screen).
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:360:- **Render scale and upscaling** (Godot-only, the Graphics detail setting; `SCNView.ApplyRenderScaling`). At `SceneKitCalibration.RenderScale` 1 (Graphics detail Max) an `SCNView`'s viewport renders at the drawable's size with `Msaa3D` from `antialiasingMode`, as before. Below 1 the 3D scene is drawn at that fraction of the drawable's width and height and upscaled to it by Godot (`Viewport.Scaling3DMode`/`Scaling3DScale`): by default with a temporal upscaler, chosen once from what the device offers (`Upscalers`, printed at first use): MetalFX temporal on the Metal driver when the device supports it at that scale (this M2: input scales 0.333-1), else FSR 2.2 (every RenderingDevice driver: Metal, Direct3D 12, Vulkan), else bilinear (no RenderingDevice). Both temporal upscalers accumulate jittered frames (Godot's jitter sequence of 8 / scale^2 phases, its mipmap bias of log2(scale), motion vectors from the depth reprojection plus a motion pass for moved instances) and replace 3D MSAA, which the facade turns off for them (Godot turns it off under MetalFX temporal itself, with a warning). `RenderUpscaler` 1-4 selects bilinear, FSR 1, MetalFX spatial or FSR 2 instead (measurements). Godot upscales after the transparent pass, so glow and tone mapping run at the drawable's size, and the AppKit overlays (HUD, menus, loading screen) are separate controls drawn over the view's texture: they stay at full resolution. `SceneKitCalibration.AnisotropicFiltering` sets the viewports' anisotropy level and `MeshLodThreshold` their mesh LOD threshold. The SSAO port keeps its disk's footprint at the drawable's size (its radius in pixels is scaled by the render scale, so the occlusion keeps its world size), and `SsaoEnabled` false skips it (the effect stops asking Godot for the normal-roughness buffer and clears `scn_ssao` to 1). Under a temporal upscaler `snapshot()` draws the view once per jitter phase (at most 32) so the upscaler's history converges on the still view, as on screen when the camera rests. `SCNRenderer` (offscreen snapshots of the test modes) always renders at full resolution with MSAA.
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:363:- `SCNView`/`SCNRenderer.prepare(_:completionHandler:)` is asynchronous, as in SceneKit (`SceneKitRuntime.PrepareAsync`): the scene's mesh arrays and procedural textures (mipmaps) are computed on worker threads, the main thread hands the nodes whose data is ready to Godot for at most 10 ms per frame, and the handler runs when all of them are flushed; the game keeps the loading screen up meanwhile. `prepare(_:shouldAbortBlock:)`, snapshots and `SCNTransaction.flush()` flush everything at once (`FlushAll`). Material properties whose contents are `res://` image paths start loading the imported texture on Godot's loader threads when the contents are set (`NSImage.Preload`), so a scene built on a background queue finds them loaded.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Reflection;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Godot;

namespace Marvin;

/// Marks a static method `Task Run(string dir, SceneTree tree)` (or `void Run(...)`) as a command-line
/// mode, e.g. [GameMode("--town-smoke-test")]. Main runs it when the flag is passed after "--":
///   tools/godot -- --town-smoke-test captures/town
/// Mirror the macOS flag names and output file names so captures can be compared side by side.
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method, AllowMultiple = true)]
public sealed class GameModeAttribute : Attribute
{
    public string Flag { get; }
    public GameModeAttribute(string flag) { Flag = flag; }
}

public static class GameModes
{
    static Dictionary<string, MethodInfo> modes;

    public static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, MethodInfo> All
    {
        get
        {
            if (modes != null) return modes;
            modes = new Dictionary<string, MethodInfo>();
            foreach (var type in typeof(GameModes).Assembly.GetTypes())
                foreach (var method in type.GetMethods(BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic))
                    foreach (var attribute in method.GetCustomAttributes<GameModeAttribute>())
                    {
                        if (modes.ContainsKey(attribute.Flag)) throw new InvalidOperationException($"duplicate game mode {attribute.Flag}");
                        modes[attribute.Flag] = method;
                    }
            return modes;
        }
    }

    /// Resolves a mode's output directory like the macOS app: relative paths are relative to the working directory.
    public static string OutputDirectory(string arg, string fallback)
    {
        string dir = string.IsNullOrEmpty(arg) || arg.StartsWith("--") ? fallback : arg;
        // The modes write with System.IO, which does not know Godot's user:// (it would create a "user:" folder).
        if (dir.StartsWith("user://")) dir = ProjectSettings.GlobalizePath(dir);
        if (!dir.StartsWith("res://") && !dir.StartsWith("user://") && !System.IO.Path.IsPathRooted(dir))
            dir = System.IO.Path.GetFullPath(dir, System.IO.Directory.GetCurrentDirectory());
        if (!dir.StartsWith("res://") && !dir.StartsWith("user://")) System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(dir);
        return dir;
    }

    /// Runs the first registered mode found in args. Returns false when no mode flag is present.
    public static async Task<bool> TryRun(string[] args, SceneTree tree)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < args.Length; i++)
        {
            if (!All.TryGetValue(args[i], out var method)) continue;
            string dir = OutputDirectory(i + 1 < args.Length ? args[i + 1] : null, "user://" + args[i].TrimStart('-'));
            var result = method.Invoke(null, new object[] { dir, tree });
            if (result is Task task) await task;
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}

apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:257:**Graphics-detail variants** (Godot-only, look changes, never at Graphics detail Max; `SceneKitRuntime.DetailVariant`, "Known deviations"). `SceneKitCalibration.SimpleSkyReflection` adds `VariantFlags.SimpleSky` to every scene's variant: physically based materials whose roughness no shader modifier changes (everything but the robots, whose `DirtCoating` modifier writes `ROUGHNESS`, so their chrome keeps the sharp horizon of the radiance bands) take their sky reflection from the sky light's spherical harmonics at the reflection direction (`scn_irradiance(scn_refl)`) instead of `scn_env_radiance` (the equirect mapping and two texture fetches). `SimpleGroundLighting` adds `VariantFlags.SimpleGround`: blended physically based materials that write no depth (the town's ground overlays: trampled sand, streets, doorway patches, aprons) get no direct specular term in `light()` and the same spherical-harmonics sky reflection. A change at run time bumps `SceneKitRuntime.DetailEpoch`; each scene rebuilds its nodes with the new variants before a view draws it next (`ObserveShading`) or when it is prepared (`PrepareAsync`: a race world cached from an earlier race rebuilds behind the loading screen).
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:360:- **Render scale and upscaling** (Godot-only, the Graphics detail setting; `SCNView.ApplyRenderScaling`). At `SceneKitCalibration.RenderScale` 1 (Graphics detail Max) an `SCNView`'s viewport renders at the drawable's size with `Msaa3D` from `antialiasingMode`, as before. Below 1 the 3D scene is drawn at that fraction of the drawable's width and height and upscaled to it by Godot (`Viewport.Scaling3DMode`/`Scaling3DScale`): by default with a temporal upscaler, chosen once from what the device offers (`Upscalers`, printed at first use): MetalFX temporal on the Metal driver when the device supports it at that scale (this M2: input scales 0.333-1), else FSR 2.2 (every RenderingDevice driver: Metal, Direct3D 12, Vulkan), else bilinear (no RenderingDevice). Both temporal upscalers accumulate jittered frames (Godot's jitter sequence of 8 / scale^2 phases, its mipmap bias of log2(scale), motion vectors from the depth reprojection plus a motion pass for moved instances) and replace 3D MSAA, which the facade turns off for them (Godot turns it off under MetalFX temporal itself, with a warning). `RenderUpscaler` 1-4 selects bilinear, FSR 1, MetalFX spatial or FSR 2 instead (measurements). Godot upscales after the transparent pass, so glow and tone mapping run at the drawable's size, and the AppKit overlays (HUD, menus, loading screen) are separate controls drawn over the view's texture: they stay at full resolution. `SceneKitCalibration.AnisotropicFiltering` sets the viewports' anisotropy level and `MeshLodThreshold` their mesh LOD threshold. The SSAO port keeps its disk's footprint at the drawable's size (its radius in pixels is scaled by the render scale, so the occlusion keeps its world size), and `SsaoEnabled` false skips it (the effect stops asking Godot for the normal-roughness buffer and clears `scn_ssao` to 1). Under a temporal upscaler `snapshot()` draws the view once per jitter phase (at most 32) so the upscaler's history converges on the still view, as on screen when the camera rests. `SCNRenderer` (offscreen snapshots of the test modes) always renders at full resolution with MSAA.
apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md:363:- `SCNView`/`SCNRenderer.prepare(_:completionHandler:)` is asynchronous, as in SceneKit (`SceneKitRuntime.PrepareAsync`): the scene's mesh arrays and procedural textures (mipmaps) are computed on worker threads, the main thread hands the nodes whose data is ready to Godot for at most 10 ms per frame, and the handler runs when all of them are flushed; the game keeps the loading screen up meanwhile. `prepare(_:shouldAbortBlock:)`, snapshots and `SCNTransaction.flush()` flush everything at once (`FlushAll`). Material properties whose contents are `res://` image paths start loading the imported texture on Godot's loader threads when the contents are set (`NSImage.Preload`), so a scene built on a background queue finds them loaded.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Reflection;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Godot;

namespace Marvin;

/// Marks a static method `Task Run(string dir, SceneTree tree)` (or `void Run(...)`) as a command-line
/// mode, e.g. [GameMode("--town-smoke-test")]. Main runs it when the flag is passed after "--":
///   tools/godot -- --town-smoke-test captures/town
/// Mirror the macOS flag names and output file names so captures can be compared side by side.
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method, AllowMultiple = true)]
public sealed class GameModeAttribute : Attribute
{
    public string Flag { get; }
    public GameModeAttribute(string flag) { Flag = flag; }
}

public static class GameModes
{
    static Dictionary<string, MethodInfo> modes;

    public static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, MethodInfo> All
    {
        get
        {
            if (modes != null) return modes;
            modes = new Dictionary<string, MethodInfo>();
            foreach (var type in typeof(GameModes).Assembly.GetTypes())
                foreach (var method in type.GetMethods(BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic))
                    foreach (var attribute in method.GetCustomAttributes<GameModeAttribute>())
                    {
                        if (modes.ContainsKey(attribute.Flag)) throw new InvalidOperationException($"duplicate game mode {attribute.Flag}");
                        modes[attribute.Flag] = method;
                    }
            return modes;
        }
    }

    /// Resolves a mode's output directory like the macOS app: relative paths are relative to the working directory.
    public static string OutputDirectory(string arg, string fallback)
    {
        string dir = string.IsNullOrEmpty(arg) || arg.StartsWith("--") ? fallback : arg;
        // The modes write with System.IO, which does not know Godot's user:// (it would create a "user:" folder).
        if (dir.StartsWith("user://")) dir = ProjectSettings.GlobalizePath(dir);
        if (!dir.StartsWith("res://") && !dir.StartsWith("user://") && !System.IO.Path.IsPathRooted(dir))
            dir = System.IO.Path.GetFullPath(dir, System.IO.Directory.GetCurrentDirectory());
        if (!dir.StartsWith("res://") && !dir.StartsWith("user://")) System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(dir);
        return dir;
    }

    /// Runs the first registered mode found in args. Returns false when no mode flag is present.
    public static async Task<bool> TryRun(string[] args, SceneTree tree)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < args.Length; i++)
        {
            if (!All.TryGetValue(args[i], out var method)) continue;
            string dir = OutputDirectory(i + 1 < args.Length ? args[i + 1] : null, "user://" + args[i].TrimStart('-'));
            var result = method.Invoke(null, new object[] { dir, tree });
            if (result is Task task) await task;
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}
